findings.description: Background color is hardcoded as #ffffff instead of using the Colors.light.surface token, which will not adapt to dark mode, leaving text invisible on dark surfaces.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace backgroundColor: '#ffffff' with backgroundColor: colors.surface using the ThemeColors token from useColorScheme.

findings.description: Border color is hardcoded as #E5E7EB (Gray 200), bypassing the Colors.light.border token and failing to adapt in dark mode where it will be near-invisible against dark surfaces.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace borderColor: '#E5E7EB' with borderColor: colors.border.

findings.description: A nearly transparent white (#ffffff11) is used as the card background; on a dark background (#0F172A) this resolves to an extremely low-luminance surface that will make any dark-mode text (#F1F5F9) nearly invisible against other surrounding elements, and in light mode renders as nearly transparent.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace backgroundColor: '#ffffff11' with backgroundColor: colors.surface to get an opaque, theme-aware card background.

findings.description: Input text and background are both hardcoded hex values that will not adapt to dark mode, causing near-black text on a dark surface background in dark mode.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace color: '#111827' with color: colors.text and backgroundColor: '#FFFFFF' with backgroundColor: colors.surface.

findings.description: The hardcoded Slate 600 (#475569) achieves 6.86:1 on white in light mode but only approximately 3.17:1 against the dark background #0F172A, failing WCAG AA for normal text.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace color: '#475569' with color: colors.textSecondary so the dark-mode value (#94A3B8, 5.27:1) is used automatically.

findings.description: dismiss text uses hardcoded #4B5563 (Gray 600) which passes light mode but is not token-driven and will not adapt to dark mode where it falls below AA against dark surfaces.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace color: '#4B5563' with color: colors.textSecondary.

findings.description: The ghost CTA text uses brand primary teal (#0D9488) at font-size 13px, which only achieves 3.06:1 contrast — failing WCAG AA for normal-weight text at this size.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace color: '#0D9488' with color: Colors.light.tint applied only for large/bold text, or use Colors.brand.primaryDeep (#115E59, 5.87:1) for normal-weight small text.

findings.description: lossSummary uses a hardcoded near-black background #0b1224 which is not a design token and will not respond to theme changes; text rendered inside at default light-mode color (#0F172A) would be approximately 1.02:1 — essentially invisible.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace backgroundColor: '#0b1224' with a token-driven surface (e.g., colors.surface or Colors.dark.background) and ensure text inside uses colors.text explicitly.

findings.description: The draftStatus text color #92400e achieves approximately 4.32:1 against the light background, narrowly failing WCAG AA for normal text.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace color: '#92400e' with color: Colors.light.warning (#B45309, 4.82:1) which is the correct token for warning-level text.

findings.description: All banner background variants are hardcoded light-mode surface colors (#EFF6FF, #ECFDF3, #FEF2F2, #FFFBEB) with no dark-mode equivalent, so banners will appear with light pastel backgrounds in dark mode.
findings.proposed_fix: Drive banner backgrounds from theme tokens: use colors.successSurface, colors.errorSurface, colors.warningSurface, and a blue equivalent referencing brand.proSurface or a dynamic style object.

findings.description: Tag chip background is a hardcoded light-mode pastel that does not adapt to dark mode, potentially rendering text invisible on dark surfaces.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace backgroundColor: '#eef2ff' with a token-driven surface; use brand.proSurface for light and Colors.dark.surfaceRaised for dark, driven via dynamic styles.

findings.description: Badge background is a hardcoded light-mode tint that will not adapt in dark mode, and no text color is explicitly set on the badge, creating potential contrast failures.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace with a token pair: backgroundColor: colors.successSurface or a computed dynamic style, and explicitly set badgeText color to colors.text.

findings.description: Disabled state is communicated only via 0.6 opacity reduction; at reduced opacity on primaryButton (#2563EB) the resulting effective ratio may fall below 3:1, and opacity alone is insufficient for users who cannot perceive contrast differences.
findings.proposed_fix: Supplement opacity reduction with a distinct background token, e.g., backgroundColor: colors.border, and color: colors.textTertiary, to communicate disabled state without relying solely on opacity.

findings.description: The lossSummary card uses a light-mode border (#E5E7EB) against a hardcoded dark background (#0b1224), achieving approximately 1.39:1 — essentially invisible as a boundary indicator.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace borderColor: '#E5E7EB' with colors.border and align the background to a proper dark-mode token as noted in SS-008.

findings.description: The status color passes AA in light mode but is a hardcoded value not mapped to a design token, and will not adapt for dark mode where it will be far too dark against dark surfaces.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace color: '#065f46' with color: colors.success (which uses #15803D in light and #34D399 in dark).

findings.description: publishedStatus uses hardcoded Green 700 (#15803D) which achieves 5.44:1 in light mode but only approximately 3.38:1 against the dark background, failing WCAG AA.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace color: '#15803d' with color: colors.success, which correctly maps to #34D399 in dark mode (high contrast on dark bg).

findings.description: Text at 13px is below the recommended 16px body minimum and is particularly problematic for outdoor/ambient-light mobile use where smaller text becomes illegible.
findings.proposed_fix: Increase fontSize to at least 14 (bold) or 16 (normal weight) to meet minimum legibility guidelines.

findings.description: At 12px this text is at the absolute minimum legible floor; while contrast is marginal at 4.35:1 for this size, ambient-light conditions on mobile will reduce effective legibility significantly.
findings.proposed_fix: Increase fontSize to 13 or 14 and consider using colors.textSecondary (#475569 / #94A3B8) to ensure reliable dark-mode contrast.

findings.description: toggleChip uses paddingVertical: 8 with no explicit minHeight, resulting in a touch target likely below the recommended 44px minimum height for interactive elements.
findings.proposed_fix: Add minHeight: 44 to toggleChip style to ensure the tap target meets WCAG 2.5.5 and Apple/Google HIG guidelines.

findings.description: If tags are interactive, paddingVertical: 4 will produce a touch target well below 44px, posing an accessibility concern for motor-impaired users.
findings.proposed_fix: If tags are tappable, increase paddingVertical to at least 10 or add minHeight: 44.

findings.description: The done-state indicator border (#22C55E) against its own background (#DCFCE7) achieves only approximately 1.51:1, making the completion state boundary poorly visible for low-vision users.
findings.proposed_fix: Use a darker border such as #15803D (Green 700) or Colors.light.success for the done-state border to achieve at least 3:1 against #DCFCE7.

findings.description: backgroundColor '#ffffff11' is a raw semi-transparent hex that renders differently on every theme surface — it is not a design token and creates an unpredictable background that can undermine all child text contrast ratios.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace with Colors.light.surface / Colors.dark.surface via useColorScheme: backgroundColor: colorScheme === 'dark' ? Colors.dark.surface : Colors.light.surface

findings.description: Same raw semi-transparent '#ffffff11' used for MetricCard background creates undefined rendering substrate for all KPI text, especially in dark mode where it blends into the dark surface unpredictably.
findings.proposed_fix: Use Colors.light.surface / Colors.dark.surface token via useColorScheme, same as EXP-001.

findings.description: #EF4444 (Red 500) at 3.45:1 on white fails WCAG AA for normal-size body text.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace hardcoded '#EF4444' with Colors.light.error (#DC2626, 4.64:1) via token: color: colors.error

findings.element: errorText — error message body text in dark mode
findings.description: errorText is hardcoded '#EF4444' which narrowly passes in dark mode (4.55:1) but fails in light mode (3.45:1); it should use the theme-aware error token to be correct in both modes.
findings.proposed_fix: Use colors.error token from useColorScheme: in light mode Colors.light.error=#DC2626, in dark mode Colors.dark.error=#F87171.

findings.description: Button color #2563EB is hardcoded and not a design token — it deviates from the Horario teal brand primary and will not update if the design system changes.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace '#2563EB' with brand.primary (#0D9488) or brand.primaryDark (#0F766E); white text on #0F766E is 9.30:1 AAA. Use token: backgroundColor: Colors.light.tint (or brand.primaryDark for higher contrast).

findings.description: primaryButton also uses hardcoded '#2563EB' — same off-brand, non-tokenized issue as retryButton; inconsistent with the teal design system.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace with brand.primaryDark (#0F766E): backgroundColor: brand.primaryDark. White text yields 9.30:1 AAA.

findings.description: #2563EB bar fill vs #E5E7EB track background is 2.19:1, failing WCAG 1.4.11 non-text contrast (3:1 required for UI components).
findings.proposed_fix: Replace barFill backgroundColor '#2563EB' with brand.primaryDeep (#115E59) which achieves ≥3:1 against #E5E7EB, or use brand.primaryDark (#0F766E). Also replace barTrack '#E5E7EB' with Colors.light.border (#E2E8F0) token.

findings.description: metricSub and mutedText are hardcoded to '#475569' (Slate 600) which is 6.86:1 on white (light mode ✓) but only 3.11:1 on the dark surface #1E293B, failing AA for 12px normal text.
findings.proposed_fix: Drive color through theme token: use colors.textSecondary (light: #475569, dark: #94A3B8 = 5.27:1 on dark). Remove hardcoded hex from StyleSheet and apply via dynamic style.

findings.description: Same dark-mode contrast failure as metricSub — mutedText at '#475569' drops to 3.11:1 on dark surfaces, failing AA.
findings.proposed_fix: Same fix as EXP-008: replace with colors.textSecondary token dynamically per theme.

findings.description: barTrack is hardcoded '#E5E7EB' (light gray) — it will appear very bright against dark surfaces, looking visually inverted and clashing with dark mode palette.
findings.proposed_fix: Use Colors.light.border / Colors.dark.border tokens via useColorScheme: backgroundColor: colorScheme === 'dark' ? Colors.dark.border : Colors.light.border

findings.description: fairnessBarTrack has the same hardcoded '#E5E7EB' issue — inverted appearance in dark mode and unverifiable non-text contrast against the dynamic bar fill colors.
findings.proposed_fix: Use Colors.dark.border (#334155) in dark mode, Colors.light.border (#E2E8F0) in light mode via useColorScheme token.

findings.description: #22C55E (Green 500) against the '#E5E7EB' track achieves only ~1.77:1, failing WCAG 1.4.11 non-text contrast; the bar fill is a meaningful UI component conveying fairness status.
findings.proposed_fix: For the excellent/green bar fill, use '#15803D' (Green 700) which achieves ≥3:1 against #E5E7EB, or use brand.success token from Colors.light.success.

findings.description: #F59E0B (Amber 400) on '#E5E7EB' achieves only ~1.73:1, failing WCAG 1.4.11 non-text contrast for the 'good' fairness state bar.
findings.proposed_fix: Use '#D97706' (Amber 600, brand.accentDark) or '#B45309' (Amber 700) for the bar fill to achieve ≥3:1 against the track. Against #E5E7EB, Amber 700 #B45309 achieves ~3.3:1.

findings.description: Pressable buttons have no pressed, focused, or hovered visual state (no style callback, no ripple, no opacity change), making state changes invisible to users who rely on visible focus indicators (WCAG 2.4.11).
findings.proposed_fix: Pass a style function to Pressable: style={({ pressed }) => [styles.primaryButton, pressed && { opacity: 0.8 }]} and add focusable/accessible props; also add a visible focus ring via outlineWidth/outlineColor on web.

findings.description: metricLabel at 13px is below the recommended 16px minimum body text size for comfortable reading, especially in outdoor/ambient light conditions.
findings.proposed_fix: Increase to fontSize: 14 at minimum, ideally 15–16 for labels that carry meaningful information.

findings.description: metricSub at 12px with no lineHeight set is below minimum recommended size and line-height (should be ≥1.5× font-size = 18 for 12px text).
findings.proposed_fix: Set fontSize: 13, lineHeight: 20 (≥1.5× 13px); align with Colors.light.textSecondary token.

findings.description: retryButton uses paddingVertical: 10, yielding approximately 38px total height with default text — below the recommended 44px minimum touch target for mobile accessibility.
findings.proposed_fix: Increase to paddingVertical: 14 or add minHeight: 44 to the button style to meet WCAG 2.5.5 target size guidance.

findings.description: metricValue has lineHeight 34 for fontSize 28, giving a 1.21× ratio — below the WCAG recommended 1.5× line-height for body-equivalent text (though large display text is exempt, sub-text proximity may be tight).
findings.proposed_fix: Increase lineHeight to 42 (1.5× of 28) or at minimum 38 for comfortable vertical rhythm in the KPI card.

findings.description: `backgroundColor: '#ffffff11'` (≈4% white alpha) renders as an unpredictable tint whose effective colour depends on the surface beneath, bypasses design tokens, and in dark mode produces near-invisible cards on the dark background (#0F172A).
findings.proposed_fix: Replace with `backgroundColor: Colors[scheme].surface` (light: `#FFFFFF`, dark: `#1E293B`) via `useColorScheme` or use `ThemedView` which already maps to the correct surface token.

findings.description: The primary CTA uses a hardcoded `#2563EB` (Blue 600) that is not part of the Horario design token system; it will never respond to theme changes and deviates from the teal brand palette.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace `backgroundColor: '#2563EB'` with `backgroundColor: brand.primaryDark` (`#0F766E`); white text on `#0F766E` gives 9.30:1 ✅ AAA and aligns with brand identity.

findings.description: While text contrast is technically fine, the near-invisible card container provides no visual separation from the dark page background, making card boundaries imperceptible and causing STATE_VISIBILITY failure for interactive cards.
findings.proposed_fix: Use `Colors.dark.surface` (`#1E293B`) as the card background in dark mode so cards are visually distinct from the `#0F172A` page background.

findings.description: Light mode ratio is acceptable, but in dark mode `#475569` on dark surface (`#1E293B` ≈ 2.17:1) fails AA — the hardcoded value cannot adapt to dark mode.
findings.proposed_fix: Remove hardcoded `color: '#475569'` and use `color: Colors[scheme].textSecondary` — dark mode token `#94A3B8` achieves 5.27:1 on `#1E293B` ✅ AA.

findings.element: emptyStateCtaText — teal link text on card surface
findings.description: `color: '#0D9488'` at 14px normal weight achieves only 3.06:1 on white, failing WCAG AA normal text (requires 4.5:1); it passes only for text ≥18pt or bold ≥14pt.
findings.proposed_fix: Use `color: brand.primaryDeep` (`#115E59`, 5.87:1 ✅ AA) or `Colors.light.tint` paired with `fontWeight: '700'` and `fontSize: 16` to qualify as large/bold text at 3:1 minimum.

findings.element: emptyStateCtaText — teal link text in dark mode
findings.description: The hardcoded `#0D9488` teal on dark surface `#1E293B` yields approximately 2.54:1, failing AA in dark mode for normal text.
findings.proposed_fix: Use `Colors[scheme].tint` which resolves to `#2DD4BF` in dark mode — white/dark-surface contrast is 8.95:1 ✅ AAA.

findings.element: heroTagline text on parallax header background
findings.description: The 80% opacity white reduces effective luminance; while ratios are technically AA-passing on the solid header colors, parallax motion and any lighter image overlay can push contrast below threshold.
findings.proposed_fix: Use fully opaque `color: '#FFFFFF'` to guarantee contrast under all parallax conditions, matching `heroWordmark` and `heroLogoText`.

findings.description: Both `backgroundColor: '#ffffff'` and `borderColor: '#E5E7EB'` are hardcoded and will not adapt in dark mode, leaving buttons invisible on dark surfaces with a near-zero background contrast.
findings.proposed_fix: Use `backgroundColor: Colors[scheme].surface` and `borderColor: Colors[scheme].border` (`#E2E8F0` light / `#334155` dark) resolved via `useColorScheme`.

findings.description: The `Pressable` primaryButton has no `style` callback for pressed state, so users receive no visual feedback on activation beyond the OS ripple/opacity flash, which may be suppressed on some platforms.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `style={({ pressed }) => [styles.primaryButton, pressed && { opacity: 0.75 }]}` and optionally a `disabled` style with `backgroundColor: Colors.light.border` and `color: Colors.light.textTertiary`.

findings.description: The three quick-action `Pressable` elements lack pressed-state styles, making them visually indistinguishable from static `View` containers during interaction.
findings.proposed_fix: Apply `style={({ pressed }) => [styles.actionButton, pressed && { backgroundColor: Colors[scheme].background }]}` to provide a distinct pressed affordance.

findings.element: heroLogoMark — semi-transparent white border and background on dark header
findings.description: `rgba(255,255,255,0.2)` fill and `rgba(255,255,255,0.35)` border on the dark header (`#134E4A`) produce an effective luminance contrast of approximately 1.8:1, failing the 3:1 non-text / UI component minimum.
findings.proposed_fix: In dark mode use `backgroundColor: 'rgba(255,255,255,0.30)'` and `borderColor: 'rgba(255,255,255,0.55)'` or switch to a solid `brand.primaryLight` (`#99F6E4`) tint to achieve ≥3:1.

findings.description: Even if the colour is corrected, 14px normal-weight text is below the recommended 16px minimum body size for outdoor/mobile readability and below the 18pt threshold for AA-Large exemption.
findings.proposed_fix: Increase to `fontSize: 16` or add `fontWeight: '600'` and ensure the corrected colour meets 4.5:1 at the smaller size.

findings.element: card gap/padding — touch target for shift rows
findings.description: The `rowBetween` shift rows have no explicit `minHeight`, making the touch target for badge/pill elements potentially below the 44pt minimum on small-density screens.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `minHeight: 44` to `styles.rowBetween` to guarantee minimum touch target height per WCAG 2.5.5.

findings.description: The tagline has `fontSize: 14` but no `lineHeight`, defaulting to ~17px line-height (1.2× ratio), below the WCAG recommended 1.5× (21px) for body/label text.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `lineHeight: 21` (1.5 × 14) to `styles.heroTagline` to meet best-practice line-height guidance.

findings.description: The semi-transparent #ffffff11 background composites unpredictably over whatever surface is beneath it, making all child text contrast unverifiable and potentially failing in dark mode or over image backgrounds.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace with `backgroundColor: Colors[scheme].surface` (opaque token) or `Colors[scheme].surfaceRaised`, eliminating the semi-transparent layer; if a tinted card is desired use `brand.primarySurface` (#F0FDFA) in light mode.

findings.element: helperText — streak helper / reward message body text
findings.description: Although #475569 (Slate 600) gives 6.86:1 on a pure white surface, the actual backing colour is the semi-transparent #ffffff11 container over an unknown parent, so the true ratio is unverifiable; in dark mode the ThemedText colour override does not apply so dark-mode text defaults will render against this hardcoded light value.
findings.proposed_fix: Remove the inline `color: '#475569'` hardcode and instead apply `color: Colors[scheme].textSecondary` via a theme-aware style, and resolve SC-001 to establish a known background.

findings.description: The hardcoded light-mode Slate 600 colour (#475569) achieves only ~3.0:1 against the dark-mode background (#0F172A), a clear AA failure for body text in dark mode.
findings.proposed_fix: Use `color: Colors[scheme].textSecondary` which resolves to #475569 in light and #94A3B8 (5.27:1) in dark mode.

findings.description: #dbeafe is a hardcoded hex not from the design token system; ThemedText default text colour in dark mode is #F1F5F9 which gives approximately 1.05:1 against #dbeafe — a critical contrast failure.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace `backgroundColor: '#dbeafe'` with `brand.proSurface` (#F5F3FF) or `brand.primarySurface` (#F0FDFA) and set explicit badge text colour to `Colors[scheme].text` (or `brand.primaryDeep` #115E59 at 5.87:1 on those surfaces).

findings.element: badge — dark mode text on #dbeafe background
findings.description: In dark mode ThemedText renders #F1F5F9 text on the hardcoded #dbeafe badge background, which is near-white-on-white and completely illegible.
findings.proposed_fix: Conditionally set badge background per scheme: light → `brand.primarySurface`, dark → `brand.primaryDeep`; fix badgeText colour to `brand.primaryDeep` (light) / `brand.primaryLight` (dark) using themed tokens.

findings.description: #2563EB (Blue 600) on #E5E7EB (Gray 200) track achieves 3.71:1 which passes the 3:1 non-text threshold, but both colours are hardcoded hex values outside the token system; in dark mode #E5E7EB track is very light against a dark background, creating a jarring unthemed element.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace `backgroundColor: '#2563EB'` with `brand.primary` (#0D9488) for brand consistency, and replace track `backgroundColor: '#E5E7EB'` with `Colors[scheme].border` for dark-mode compatibility.

findings.description: The reward card background is hardcoded to #f8fafc (near-white); in dark mode ThemedText renders light text (#F1F5F9) against it, producing ~1.06:1 — completely unreadable.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace `backgroundColor: '#f8fafc'` with `Colors[scheme].surface` and `borderColor: '#E5E7EB'` with `Colors[scheme].border` using a scheme-aware style.

findings.description: The disabled state uses only `opacity: 0.7` which still passes contrast, but provides no distinct visual language (no colour change, no pattern) to communicate the disabled/completed state beyond slight dimming; additionally opacity stacks with any parent transparency.
findings.proposed_fix: For the disabled state, change `backgroundColor` to `Colors[scheme].border` (#E2E8F0 light / #334155 dark) and `color` to `Colors[scheme].textTertiary` to clearly communicate an inactive state, removing reliance on opacity alone.

findings.description: #111827 hardcodes a near-black button that ignores the design token system; in dark mode this creates a very dark button that visually recedes into the dark background (#0F172A), reducing affordance.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace `backgroundColor: '#111827'` with `Colors[scheme].tint` (light: #0D9488, dark: #2DD4BF) so the CTA button uses on-brand primary colour with white text (6.88:1 / 8.95:1 respectively).

findings.description: The hardcoded #111827 button background is nearly indistinguishable from the dark-mode page background #0F172A (contrast ~1.12:1), making the interactive element invisible as a separate affordance.
findings.proposed_fix: Use `Colors[scheme].tint` as button background (see SC-009); this gives a clearly visible teal button in dark mode (#2DD4BF on #0F172A = 8.95:1).

findings.description: All text and interactive elements inside the container inherit an unresolvable background due to the semi-transparent #ffffff11 layer; automated contrast checking tools cannot verify compliance and actual ratios depend entirely on runtime parent rendering.
findings.proposed_fix: Use an opaque background token (e.g. `Colors[scheme].surface`) so all child contrast ratios are deterministic; if a frosted-glass effect is required, add a guaranteed minimum-luminance solid base layer.

findings.description: #E5E7EB is hardcoded and does not adapt to dark mode, where the light grey track against a dark background may appear overly bright and inconsistent with the design system.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace `backgroundColor: '#E5E7EB'` with `Colors[scheme].border` (#E2E8F0 light / #334155 dark).

findings.description: The progress bar is only 10px tall, which may be difficult to perceive or interact with for users with low vision or motor impairments; WCAG 2.5.8 recommends minimum 24px for non-text targets.
findings.proposed_fix: Increase `height` to at least 12–16px for better visual weight, and consider adding an `accessibilityValueText` prop to the progressbar for screen reader numeric announcement.

findings.description: The button has `paddingVertical: 12` which may produce a touch target below the recommended 44px minimum height depending on font size and line height.
findings.proposed_fix: Set `minHeight: 44` on `logButton` style to guarantee the WCAG 2.5.5 / Apple HIG minimum touch target regardless of text size.

findings.description: The helperText style sets no explicit lineHeight; ThemedText default may produce sub-1.5× line spacing for multi-line helper strings, reducing readability per WCAG 1.4.12.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `lineHeight: 22` (≈1.57× a default 14px size) to `helperText` style, or use a consistent body token such as `{ fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 22 }`.

findings.description: White text on Emerald 500 badge background yields only 3.46:1, failing WCAG AA for normal-sized text (11px bold is still below 18pt/14pt-bold threshold for large-text exemption).
findings.proposed_fix: Change trialBadge backgroundColor to brand.successSurface is insufficient; instead darken the badge to Colors.light.success (#15803D) which gives 5.44:1 vs white: `backgroundColor: '#15803D'` — or use `Colors.light.success` token.

findings.element: trialText — body sentence on successSurface (#ECFDF5) background
findings.description: brand.primaryDeep (#115E59) at 13px yields 5.87:1 on successSurface — this passes AA. No issue here; listed only to confirm correctness. (Finding suppressed — see UB-003 for the actual sibling failure.)
findings.proposed_fix: No change required; keep brand.primaryDeep for trialText.

findings.element: trialSub — '$12/mo flat after trial.' subline on successSurface (#ECFDF5)
findings.description: brand.primaryDark (#0F766E) at 11px on successSurface (#ECFDF5) achieves only 4.01:1, failing WCAG AA for normal text; 11px is well below the large-text threshold.
findings.proposed_fix: Use brand.primaryDeep (#115E59) which yields 5.87:1 on successSurface: `color: brand.primaryDeep` in the trialSub style.

findings.description: The hardcoded hex #1E1B4B bypasses the design token system entirely; while its contrast ratio is sufficient in light mode, it will not adapt to dark mode (dark background #0F172A still passes, but the token system is bypassed, creating a maintenance risk and potential future failures).
findings.proposed_fix: Replace with a system token: `color: Colors.light.text` (or resolve via useThemeColor) — #0F172A gives 17.85:1 on proSurface and the token will adapt correctly.

findings.element: freePlanCta — CTA link text on proSurface (#F5F3FF)
findings.description: brand.pro (#7C3AED) at 12px on proSurface (#F5F3FF) yields approximately 5.05:1 — this technically passes AA, but at 12px (below 16px body minimum) the safety margin is thin and ambient-light degradation in outdoor use can push perceived contrast below threshold.
findings.proposed_fix: Increase font size to at least 13px (matching freePlanTitle) or switch to brand.proDark (#6D28D9) which yields ~6.3:1, providing a safer margin: `color: brand.proDark, fontSize: 13`.

findings.element: pricingNote — '$12/mo flat · no per-employee fees · cancel anytime'
findings.description: Hardcoded Gray 500 (#6B7280) at 11px on proSurface (#F5F3FF) achieves only ~4.40:1 — the inline comment claims 4.48:1 on proSurface but that calculation is optimistic; the actual luminance computation yields below 4.5:1, failing WCAG AA for 11px normal text. Also bypasses the token system.
findings.proposed_fix: Use `Colors.light.textSecondary` (#475569, 6.86:1 on white/proSurface) or at minimum `Colors.light.textTertiary` (#64748B, 4.35:1 — still just below AA); best fix is textSecondary at a bumped size of 12px: `color: Colors.light.textSecondary, fontSize: 12`.

findings.element: Entire UpgradeBanner component — both trial and free variants
findings.description: The component imports only from `brand` (raw palette) rather than `Colors.light/dark`, and all text colors are hardcoded; no dark-mode surface or text adaptation is implemented, so the banner will render light-mode colours on a dark background in dark mode.
findings.proposed_fix: Introduce `const colors = Colors[useColorScheme() ?? 'light']` and use `colors.text`, `colors.textSecondary`, `colors.surface`, and `colors.successSurface`/`colors.proSurface` equivalents; derive surface and border colours from Colors dark tokens.

findings.element: freeBanner border — brand.proLight (#A78BFA) border on dark-mode surface
findings.description: In dark mode, brand.proLight (#A78BFA) border on slate-800 surface (#1E293B) achieves only ~3.33:1 — barely passes non-text 3:1 but the component currently does not switch to dark mode at all (see UB-007), so this border colour against the dark background will be rendered incorrectly.
findings.proposed_fix: When dark mode is active, use `brand.proLight` (#A78BFA) for the border (acceptable) but ensure the surface behind it switches to `Colors.dark.surface` (#1E293B) via the color-scheme hook.

findings.element: freeBanner Pressable pressed state — bannerPressed applies opacity 0.85 + scale 0.99
findings.description: The pressed feedback relies solely on opacity 0.85 and scale 0.99; the scale change (1%) is imperceptible and the opacity reduction is subtle on an already light-coloured surface, providing insufficient tactile-visual confirmation especially for users with low vision or in bright ambient light.
findings.proposed_fix: Augment the pressed style with a visible background shift: `backgroundColor: brand.proLight` (or `'#EDE9FE'` Violet 100) in the pressed state, which creates a clear darkening of the surface independent of opacity.

findings.element: trialBadgeText and freeBadgeText — 11px bold ALL-CAPS labels
findings.description: Both badge labels are 11px; even with fontWeight '800' and all-caps letterSpacing, 11px does not qualify as WCAG 'large text' (requires ≥18pt/24px regular or ≥14pt/~18.67px bold), so the 3:1 large-text exemption does not apply — the TRIAL badge on #10B981 fails outright (UB-001) and the size itself is a readability risk for both badges.
findings.proposed_fix: Raise badge font size to 12px minimum and bold (which still won't reach large-text threshold but improves legibility), and fix the TRIAL badge background to #15803D as noted in UB-001.

findings.element: trialText and trialSub — line-height not specified for multi-line capable text
findings.description: Neither trialText (13px) nor trialSub (11px) specify a lineHeight; React Native defaults to ~1.2× which falls below the WCAG 1.4.8 / best-practice 1.5× recommendation for body-level reading comfort.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `lineHeight: 20` to trialText (≈1.54× of 13px) and `lineHeight: 17` to trialSub (≈1.55× of 11px).

findings.element: freePlanTitle, freePlanCta, pricingNote — no lineHeight set
findings.description: All three free-plan text elements lack explicit lineHeight, leaving React Native to apply its tight default (~1.2×), which impairs readability for users with cognitive or visual impairments.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `lineHeight: 20` to freePlanTitle (13px), `lineHeight: 19` to freePlanCta (12px), and `lineHeight: 18` to pricingNote (11px).

findings.element: pricingNote, trialSub, trialBadgeText, freeBadgeText — font sizes below 12px
findings.description: Multiple text elements use 11px, which is below the 12px practical minimum for mobile legibility on high-DPI screens and especially problematic for outdoor ambient-light use; the code comment acknowledges 10px was the previous floor but 11px still falls below the recommended 12px mobile floor.
findings.proposed_fix: Set a minimum fontSize of 12px across all visible text in the component: raise trialBadgeText, freeBadgeText, trialSub, and pricingNote all to `fontSize: 12`.

findings.description: triggerText uses brand.primary (#0D9488) hardcoded on brand.primarySurface (#F0FDFA); relative luminance of #F0FDFA ≈ 0.942 and #0D9488 ≈ 0.168, giving a ratio of ~2.97:1 which fails AA for normal-size 13px/600 text.
findings.proposed_fix: Change color to Colors.light.primaryDeep (#115E59, 5.87:1 on #F0FDFA) or Colors.light.primaryDark (#0F766E, ~4.5:1). Use useColorScheme() and pull from Colors[scheme] rather than the raw brand token.

findings.description: color: brand.primary is hardcoded on a hardcoded brand.primarySurface background; this bypasses theme tokens entirely so the fix must address both the colour token choice and the theming pattern.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace both backgroundColor and color with theme-aware tokens: backgroundColor: colors.surfaceRaised, color: colors.tint (dark mode) or colors.primaryDeep (light mode) resolved via useColorScheme().

findings.description: backgroundColor: brand.primarySurface (#F0FDFA) is a near-white surface applied unconditionally in both light and dark mode; on the dark mode page background (#0F172A) the pill background almost disappears and the teal text #0D9488 achieves only ~1.62:1 against #0F172A, a total failure.
findings.proposed_fix: Compute styles inside the component using useColorScheme(): light → backgroundColor: Colors.light.surface, dark → backgroundColor: Colors.dark.surface (#1E293B); pair with matching text colour tokens.

findings.description: borderColor is constructed via string concatenation as brand.primary+'44' producing a 27%-opacity teal; non-text UI boundaries (borders around interactive elements) must meet 3:1 against adjacent colours per WCAG 1.4.11, but this low-opacity value fails badly in both modes.
findings.proposed_fix: Use a fully-opaque token: borderColor: Colors.light.border (#E2E8F0) in light mode or Colors.dark.border (#334155) in dark mode, resolved from the active theme.

findings.description: opacity: 0.6 is applied to the 13px langEnglish text; even if ThemedText uses Colors.light.text (#0F172A, 17.85:1), multiplying by 0.6 reduces effective luminance contrast to approximately 9.7:1 in light mode — but in dark mode the base text is #F1F5F9 (15.65:1) on #1E293B, reduced by opacity 0.6 to roughly 6:1 which passes AA but just barely; however any component tree that wraps a darker surface will push this below 4.5:1, and opacity-based dimming is fragile.
findings.proposed_fix: Remove opacity: 0.6 and instead use the explicit semantic token: color: colors.textSecondary (light #475569 = 6.86:1, dark #94A3B8 = 5.27:1), providing reliable, theme-aware contrast without opacity stacking.

findings.description: langRowSelected sets backgroundColor: brand.primarySurface (#F0FDFA) unconditionally; on the dark sheet surface (#1E293B) this near-white background creates an extreme light island with no dark-mode equivalent, breaking visual consistency and potentially overwhelming low-vision users with glare.
findings.proposed_fix: Drive selected background via theme: light → Colors.light.primarySurface (#F0FDFA), dark → brand.primaryDeep (#115E59) or a teal-tinted dark token so the selected state reads as selected without a harsh light panel.

findings.description: separator backgroundColor is the hardcoded hex #E2E8F0 (Colors.light.border) rather than the token; in dark mode this produces a very visible light stripe (~11:1 on dark surface) that should instead be Colors.dark.border (#334155).
findings.proposed_fix: Move separator style into the component body using useColorScheme() and reference colors.border from the active Colors[scheme] object.

findings.description: checkmark color: brand.primary (#0D9488) is hardcoded; on the dark sheet surface #1E293B the contrast is approximately 3.83:1 which fails AA for the 18px text size (not bold ≥14pt, so normal text threshold applies), and the color does not adapt to dark mode.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace with colors.tint resolved from the active theme: in dark mode Colors.dark.tint (#2DD4BF) achieves ~8.95:1 on #1E293B (AAA), in light mode use Colors.light.primaryDeep (#115E59).

findings.description: The trigger Pressable has no pressed or focused visual style (no style callback, no android_ripple, no focus ring); WCAG 2.4.11 requires that focus indicators have sufficient contrast, and 2.4.7 requires visible keyboard focus.
findings.proposed_fix: Add style={({ pressed, focused }) => [styles.trigger, (pressed || focused) && { backgroundColor: Colors.light.primarySurface, borderColor: Colors.light.borderFocus, borderWidth: 2 }]} and supply the dark-mode equivalent via theme resolution.

findings.description: The overlay backdrop is hardcoded rgba(0,0,0,0.4); while this is a decorative scrim rather than text-bearing content, defining it as a named token keeps the design system consistent and allows tuning for light vs dark mode.
findings.proposed_fix: Define a scrim token, e.g. overlayScrim: 'rgba(0,0,0,0.5)' in Colors, and reference it here; consider lightening slightly to 'rgba(0,0,0,0.3)' in light mode.

findings.description: 13px is below the recommended 16px minimum body text size; combined with the contrast failure in LS-001 this is especially problematic for users in bright outdoor ambient light on mobile.
findings.proposed_fix: Increase triggerText fontSize to at least 14px bold (which would qualify as 'large text' at 14pt bold, reducing the threshold to 3:1) or 16px regular, and resolve the foreground colour per LS-001.

findings.description: 13px helper text with opacity reduction falls below the 16px body minimum and the opacity stacking makes ambient-light outdoor legibility unreliable even when the computed ratio nominally passes.
findings.proposed_fix: Increase fontSize to 14px minimum and replace opacity with the explicit colors.textSecondary token as suggested in LS-005.

findings.description: Card background is hardcoded #ffffff — in dark mode ThemedView will still render this white background, making dark-mode text on white instead of adapting, and bypasses the design token system entirely.
findings.proposed_fix: Remove backgroundColor from card style and let ThemedView supply Colors[scheme].surface, or pass style={{ backgroundColor: colors.surface }} from a useThemeColor hook.

findings.description: Hardcoded #6b7280 (Gray 500) achieves only ~4.08:1 on white — below the 4.5:1 AA threshold for normal body text.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace color: '#6b7280' with color: colors.textSecondary (Colors.light.textSecondary = #475569, 6.86:1) from useThemeColor; never hardcode.

findings.description: Hardcoded #6b7280 on the dark surface (#1E293B) yields ~3.11:1 — a clear AA failure for normal-sized body text in dark mode.
findings.proposed_fix: Use colors.textSecondary token which resolves to #94A3B8 in dark mode (5.27:1 on #1E293B), applied via useThemeColor.

findings.description: Border color #E5E7EB is hardcoded and will be invisible in dark mode where card background is forced white — the border distinguishing the card from its context fails non-text contrast at 1.23:1.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace borderColor: '#E5E7EB' with borderColor: colors.border (Colors.light.border = #E2E8F0, Colors.dark.border = #334155) via useThemeColor.

findings.description: Progress fill #2563EB on track #E5E7EB passes 3:1 non-text contrast in light mode, but the hardcoded colours bypass tokens and will not adapt to dark mode where the track also remains hardcoded grey, yielding degraded or untested contrast.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace with brand.primaryDark (#0F766E) for fill on a token-driven track (colors.border), or use brand.primary (#0D9488) which is the established brand tint; reference as colors.tint for fill color.

findings.description: In dark mode the track remains hardcoded #E5E7EB while surrounding surfaces are dark — the track itself will appear as a bright band and the fill contrast against it is not guaranteed to meet 3:1.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace backgroundColor: '#E5E7EB' on progressTrack with colors.border token (#334155 dark / #E2E8F0 light); use colors.tint for the fill to ensure both adapt.

findings.description: #ffffff11 is ~6.7% opaque white — its blended result depends entirely on whatever sits beneath the component; text contrast inside is unpredictable and cannot be statically guaranteed.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace backgroundColor: '#ffffff11' with a token-driven opaque or semi-opaque surface: backgroundColor: colors.surfaceRaised, or remove it and rely on ThemedView's default background.

findings.description: Progress track background #E5E7EB is hardcoded and will not respond to dark mode, appearing as an overly bright element against dark surfaces.
findings.proposed_fix: Use colors.border token instead of hardcoded #E5E7EB for the track backgroundColor.

findings.description: When progress is 0 the fill renders at 0% width and is entirely invisible — there is no visual indicator of an empty/not-started state, making started vs. not-started achievements indistinguishable.
findings.proposed_fix: Render a minimum fill width (e.g., 4px / borderRadius) or an 'empty' state label such as 'Not started' when percent === 0 to preserve state differentiation.

findings.element: helperText style — description and progress count
findings.description: helperText has no explicit fontSize or lineHeight; it inherits ThemedText defaults which may render below 16sp body size or without the recommended 1.5× line-height for body copy.
findings.proposed_fix: Add fontSize: 14, lineHeight: 21 (1.5×) to helperText style, or define a dedicated 'helper' type in ThemedText that enforces these values.

findings.description: The badge element has only fontWeight: '700' with no backgroundColor or padding — it is visually indistinct from surrounding text and may not be recognisable as a status indicator, reducing scannability especially for users with cognitive disabilities.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a pill-style background using colors.tint with white text (6.88:1), or at minimum add paddingHorizontal: 6, paddingVertical: 2, borderRadius: 99 with backgroundColor: colors.primarySurface and color: colors.tint text to visually differentiate it.

findings.description: textTertiary (#64748B) at 4.35:1 falls below the 4.5:1 AA threshold for normal-weight body text; worker.role is informational content, not a placeholder, so the placeholder exemption does not apply.
findings.proposed_fix: Use Colors.light.textSecondary (#475569, 6.86:1) for worker role text: change styles.mutedText foreground token to textSecondary.

findings.description: If badge text uses brand.primary (#0D9488) on primarySurface (#F0FDFA) the ratio is approximately 3.06:1, failing AA for normal-weight text; skill labels are informational and must meet 4.5:1.
findings.proposed_fix: Set badgeText foreground to brand.primaryDeep (#115E59, 5.87:1 on #F0FDFA) or Colors.light.text (#0F172A) on the tag surface.

findings.element: primaryButton label text (primaryButtonText) — Add Worker button
findings.description: White text on brand.primary (#0D9488) achieves 6.88:1 and passes AA; however if the button uses brand.accent (#F59E0B) as background the ratio drops to 2.25:1, which would be a critical failure — verify background token in scheduler.styles.
findings.proposed_fix: Confirm styles.primaryButton background is brand.primary (#0D9488) or brand.primaryDark (#0F766E); never use brand.accent as a button background with white text.

findings.element: bannerSuccess banner — mutedText describing next step
findings.description: textTertiary (#64748B) on successSurface (#ECFDF5) yields approximately 4.20:1, below the 4.5:1 AA threshold for normal text in the availability-saved banner.
findings.proposed_fix: Use Colors.light.textSecondary (#475569) on successSurface — contrast is approximately 6.51:1, passing AA comfortably.

findings.description: brand.success (#10B981) on successSurface (#ECFDF5) is only ~2.47:1, a clear AA failure; the banner title must be legible as a success confirmation message.
findings.proposed_fix: Set bannerText foreground to Colors.light.success (#15803D, 5.44:1 on #ECFDF5) which passes AA for normal text.

findings.element: Worker role text (mutedText) in dark mode
findings.description: Dark mode textTertiary (#64748B) on dark surface (#1E293B) collapses to approximately 2.10:1, a severe AA failure in dark mode even if light mode is borderline.
findings.proposed_fix: Use Colors.dark.textSecondary (#94A3B8, 5.27:1 on #1E293B) for role text in dark mode.

findings.element: mutedText in bannerSuccess in dark mode
findings.description: textTertiary on dark successSurface (#064E3B) is approximately 1.78:1 — effectively invisible in dark mode.
findings.proposed_fix: Use Colors.dark.text (#F1F5F9) or Colors.dark.textSecondary (#94A3B8) on dark successSurface for the next-step hint text.

findings.element: Pressable primaryButton — Add Worker — pressed/disabled state
findings.description: The Pressable for Add Worker has no style callback for pressed or disabled states, so there is no visual feedback differentiating interactive from activated/unavailable states.
findings.proposed_fix: Change style prop to a function: style={({ pressed }) => [styles.primaryButton, pressed && { opacity: 0.75, backgroundColor: Colors.light.primaryDark }]}; add a disabled prop with a reduced-opacity token when workerForm fields are empty.

findings.element: Pressable handleAvailabilitySubmit — no pressed state styling
findings.description: The availability-submit Pressable also omits a pressed-state style and has no accessibilityRole or accessibilityLabel, removing both visual and screen-reader feedback.
findings.proposed_fix: Add accessibilityRole='button' and accessibilityLabel, and apply a pressed-state style: style={({ pressed }) => [styles.primaryButton, pressed && { opacity: 0.75 }]}.

findings.description: The ghost empty-state CTA text style is not defined in the provided code; if it uses textTertiary or any muted token it risks falling below 4.5:1 — verify the resolved token.
findings.proposed_fix: Ensure ghostEmptyCtaText maps to at least Colors.light.textSecondary (#475569) for normal weight or Colors.light.text (#0F172A) for maximum clarity.

findings.element: InputField placeholders (namePlaceholder, rolePlaceholder, skillsPlaceholder, workerIdPlaceholder, dayPlaceholder, fromPlaceholder, toPlaceholder)
findings.foreground: InputField internal placeholder color — token unknown
findings.description: Placeholder text colour is set inside InputField and is not visible here; if it uses brand.primaryLight (#99F6E4) or #94A3B8 the ratio may fall below 3:1 against white.
findings.proposed_fix: Confirm InputField placeholder color is at minimum Colors.light.textTertiary (#64748B, 4.35:1) which safely exceeds the 3:1 WCAG 2.1 placeholder guidance.

findings.element: dismissText — dismiss button label in success banner
findings.description: brand.primary (#0D9488) on successSurface (#ECFDF5) is approximately 2.95:1 — below AA for a normal-weight interactive dismiss label; large/bold text would need 3:1.
findings.proposed_fix: Use brand.primaryDeep (#115E59) for dismissText on successSurface — contrast is approximately 5.59:1, comfortably passing AA.

findings.element: Publish Pressable — disabled state when shift.status === 'Published'
findings.description: The disabled publish button applies styles.disabledButton over styles.actionChipPrimary but the text style remains styles.actionChipText with no disabled-state colour change, making the disabled vs enabled states visually indistinguishable for the button label.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a conditional text style: when disabled apply a token such as Colors.light.textTertiary (#64748B) on a muted background, and ensure the disabled background uses a token ≥3:1 against that text colour. Also set accessibilityState={{ disabled: true }} explicitly.

findings.element: Unpublish Pressable — disabled state when shift.status === 'Draft'
findings.description: Identical issue to RS-001: disabled unpublish button shares the same actionChipText style as enabled state, providing no visual differentiation for users relying on colour or contrast to perceive interactivity.
findings.proposed_fix: Apply a dedicated disabledChipText style using Colors.light.textTertiary (#64748B) on the disabled button background, ensure ratio ≥3:1 for the non-text element boundary, and pass accessibilityState={{ disabled: true }}.

findings.element: Notify Pressable — disabled state when shift.notified === true
findings.description: The notified/disabled notify button uses the same actionChipText colour as the enabled state; combined with shared actionChip container shape, users cannot distinguish it from an active button by appearance alone.
findings.proposed_fix: Apply disabledChipText (Colors.light.textTertiary #64748B) when shift.notified is true and use a visually distinct disabled background token. Add accessibilityState={{ disabled: true }}.

findings.foreground: styles.actionChipText — likely white (#FFFFFF) or a teal-family colour
findings.description: If actionChipPrimary background is brand.primary (#0D9488) with white text the ratio is 6.88:1 and passes — however if actionChipText resolves to a non-white teal such as brand.primaryLight (#99F6E4) on #0D9488 the ratio drops to approximately 1.55:1, which is a severe AA failure; the unresolved token is a HIGH risk.
findings.proposed_fix: Explicitly set actionChipText to Colors.light.surface (#FFFFFF) when used on brand.primary backgrounds, yielding a confirmed 6.88:1 ratio. Never use a light teal text colour on a teal background.

findings.description: The status badge colours are defined solely in scheduler.styles and are not auditable from this file; if they use brand.primary (#0D9488, 3.06:1) or brand.accent (#F59E0B, 2.08:1) as text colours on white they fail WCAG AA for normal-size text.
findings.proposed_fix: Use Colors.light.primaryDeep (#115E59, 5.87:1) for published-status text and Colors.light.warning (#B45309, 4.82:1) for draft-status text on white backgrounds.

findings.background: styles.positiveBadge — unresolved token (likely brand.successSurface #ECFDF5 light / #064E3B dark)
findings.description: Badge text colour defined in scheduler.styles may pass in light mode using Colors.light.success (#15803D, 5.44:1 on #ECFDF5) but dark mode successSurface (#064E3B) paired with the same green text value could invert contrast significantly.
findings.proposed_fix: In dark mode set badgeText to Colors.dark.success (#34D399) against Colors.dark.successSurface (#064E3B); verify the ratio (approximately 6.2:1) and gate the token via useColorScheme.

findings.element: statusPill ThemedText (badgeText) in upcomingShifts and staffingGaps sections
findings.description: statusPill background and badgeText colour are defined in external styles; without explicit dark-mode colour branching the pill may render with insufficient contrast in dark mode if the same light-mode values are applied unchanged.
findings.proposed_fix: Ensure statusPill background uses Colors.dark.surfaceRaised (#263548) in dark mode and badgeText maps to Colors.dark.text (#F1F5F9), yielding ≥15:1.

findings.description: Skeleton/ghost loading bars are decorative but marked accessibilityElementsHidden only on the outer container; if inner bars are not also hidden and the shimmer colour is a light grey on white (e.g. #E2E8F0 on #FFFFFF = 1.22:1) they fail non-text 3:1 in both modes, especially dark mode.
findings.proposed_fix: Confirm accessibilityElementsHidden propagates to all child Views (it should in RN), and use Colors.light.border (#E2E8F0) on Colors.light.background (#F8FAFC) giving approximately 1.22:1 — acceptable only because purely decorative and fully hidden from accessibility tree. In dark mode use Colors.dark.border (#334155) on Colors.dark.surface (#1E293B).

findings.element: mutedText ThemedText (shift template/time detail in upcomingShifts)
findings.description: If mutedText maps to textTertiary (#64748B, 4.35:1) it sits below the 4.5:1 AA threshold for normal-weight body text; this is not placeholder text and therefore is not exempt.
findings.proposed_fix: Upgrade informational mutedText to Colors.light.textSecondary (#475569, 6.86:1) for body/detail text, reserving textTertiary strictly for WCAG-exempt placeholder strings.

findings.element: mutedText ThemedText (gap date detail in staffingGaps section)
findings.description: Same token issue as RS-009: gap date rendered in mutedText is informational (not placeholder) and its 4.35:1 ratio falls below the 4.5:1 AA minimum for normal text.
findings.proposed_fix: Use Colors.light.textSecondary (#475569, 6.86:1) for the date ThemedText in staffing gap rows.

findings.element: All three Pressable action chips — pressed / hover state feedback
findings.description: No style prop variant handles the pressed state (Pressable style callback with pressed boolean is not used), so users in high-ambient-light environments have no visual feedback that the button responded to touch.
findings.proposed_fix: Use the Pressable style function: style={({ pressed }) => [styles.actionChip, pressed && { opacity: 0.75, backgroundColor: Colors.light.primaryDark }]} to provide a minimum 3:1 state change against the resting state.

findings.description: The securedDot is a small circular indicator inside the badge; if its fill colour does not achieve 3:1 against the badge background it fails WCAG 1.4.11 non-text contrast, reducing the ability to perceive the status indicator in outdoor/high-glare conditions.
findings.proposed_fix: Set securedDot background to Colors.light.success (#15803D) on Colors.light.successSurface (#ECFDF5), giving approximately 4.4:1 against the surface, safely above the 3:1 non-text minimum.

findings.element: secondaryButton label — 'Save Baseline' button text via styles.primaryButtonText
findings.background: styles.secondaryButton background (unknown — likely brand.primarySurface #F0FDFA or similar light teal)
findings.description: Using styles.primaryButtonText (designed for dark-background primary buttons) on a secondaryButton surface risks a contrast failure if the secondary button has a light teal/white fill with a teal text colour; the primary teal #0D9488 on white yields only 3.06:1, failing AA for normal text.
findings.proposed_fix: Ensure styles.secondaryButton uses either white background with text colour Colors.light.primaryDeep (#115E59, 5.87:1) or a filled teal background (#0D9488) with white text (#FFFFFF, 6.88:1). Do not reuse styles.primaryButtonText on light-surface secondary buttons unless the hex is confirmed ≥4.5:1.

findings.description: Badge text rendered with brand teal or amber on a matching light surface falls below the 4.5:1 AA threshold for normal-weight body text at typical badge font sizes (≤13 px).
findings.proposed_fix: Use Colors.light.primaryDeep (#115E59, 5.87:1) or Colors.light.warning (#B45309, 4.82:1) for badge text on their respective light surfaces, and confirm font size ≥18.67px/14px bold to qualify for the 3:1 large-text threshold if a lower-contrast token must be used.

findings.element: Demand target list — styles.badgeText used as standalone required-count label (right column)
findings.description: The required-count label rendered via styles.badgeText in each demandTargets row has an insufficient contrast ratio when brand.primary is used as the text colour against the page background.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace with Colors.light.primaryDeep (#115E59) for light mode and Colors.dark.tint (#2DD4BF, which achieves ≥4.5:1 on dark surfaces) for dark mode, or use Colors.light.text with a coloured pill background that meets 3:1 as large/bold text.

findings.element: Forecast action button text when forecastActionDisabled — styles.disabledButton applied
findings.foreground: styles.primaryButtonText on disabled surface (likely #FFFFFF on a muted grey ≈ #94A3B8)
findings.computed_ratio: unknown — estimated <3:1 on common disabled greys
findings.description: Disabled buttons are not exempt from WCAG 1.4.3 contrast requirements unless they are truly non-operable and identified by other means; a light-grey disabled surface with white text frequently fails AA.
findings.proposed_fix: Use a disabled surface of at least #767676 with white text (4.54:1) or #595959 with white text (7:1), and additionally mark the Pressable with accessibilityState={{ disabled: true }} so screen readers identify the state independently of colour.

findings.element: toggleChipText on inactive toggleChip — mode selector chips ('Homogeneous' / 'Manual Counts')
findings.description: The inactive chip label using textTertiary #64748B on white achieves only 4.35:1, which fails the 4.5:1 AA threshold for normal-weight text; brand primary on white is even worse at 3.06:1.
findings.proposed_fix: Use Colors.light.textSecondary (#475569, 6.86:1) for inactive chip labels, and Colors.light.surface (#FFFFFF) or brand.primaryDeep (#115E59) for active chip text to maintain clear state differentiation.

findings.element: Active vs inactive toggleChip — fallbackMode toggle
findings.description: The selected/unselected chip states must differ by at least 3:1 in their visual presentation (WCAG 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast) and the active chip lacks an accessibilityState={{ selected: true }} prop, making the selection invisible to screen readers.
findings.proposed_fix: Add accessibilityRole='radio' and accessibilityState={{ selected: fallbackMode === 'homogeneous' }} (and equivalent for 'manual') to each Pressable chip, and ensure the active chip border/background change meets 3:1 against the inactive state.

findings.element: Forecast Pressable — disabled state communicated by colour alone
findings.description: The disabled state of the forecast button is conveyed only through the disabledButton style; no accessibilityState={{ disabled: true }} is set, so VoiceOver/TalkBack users cannot detect the disabled state.
findings.proposed_fix: Add accessibilityState={{ disabled: forecastActionDisabled }} and disabled={forecastActionDisabled} to the Pressable so the platform surfaces the state semantically, independent of colour.

findings.element: styles.fallbackBadge — badge surface and text in dark mode
findings.description: The fallbackBadge and badgeText styles are defined in a static stylesheet and are unlikely to invert for dark mode, meaning the badge may become invisible or fail contrast on Colors.dark.surface (#1E293B).
findings.proposed_fix: Move badge colours into a useThemeColor hook or pass them via ThemedText/ThemedView so they resolve to brand.primarySurface/#F0FDFA text in light and proLight/#A78BFA or tint/#2DD4BF text on dark surfaces, verifying each combination reaches 4.5:1.

findings.description: If successText uses the brand.success token (#10B981) it fails AA on white (2.88:1); the corrected light-mode token Colors.light.success (#15803D, 5.44:1) should be used instead.
findings.proposed_fix: Set styles.successText colour to Colors.light.success (#15803D) in light mode and Colors.dark.success (#34D399) in dark mode via useThemeColor.

findings.description: If errorText uses brand.error (#EF4444) it achieves only 3.45:1 on white, failing AA; the design system corrected this to Colors.light.error #DC2626 (4.64:1) but the stylesheet may not have been updated.
findings.proposed_fix: Ensure styles.errorText resolves to Colors.light.error (#DC2626) in light mode and Colors.dark.error (#F87171) in dark mode; verify the stylesheet references the corrected token.

findings.element: InputField placeholder '3' for required count — informational default value
findings.description: The placeholder '3' in the required-count field is a numeric default that users may treat as informational content; if rendered in #94A3B8 it falls to 3.0:1 which fails AA even under the placeholder exemption for text that conveys meaningful default values.
findings.proposed_fix: Either pre-populate the field with a real default value (value='3') rendered in full-contrast text, or ensure the InputField placeholder colour is at minimum textTertiary #64748B (4.35:1) and the label clearly communicates the expected default so the placeholder is purely exemplary.

findings.element: styles.divider — horizontal rule separating forecast error from target list
findings.description: The divider line colour (#E2E8F0 on #F8FAFC) achieves only ~1.36:1, below the 3:1 WCAG 1.4.11 threshold required for meaningful UI component boundaries.
findings.proposed_fix: Increase the divider to Colors.light.textTertiary (#64748B) at reduced opacity (e.g. 40%) or use a 1px border at Colors.light.border with a slightly darker token such as #CBD5E1 (Slate 300, ~1.7:1); if the divider is purely decorative add accessibilityElementsHidden={true} to exclude it from the a11y tree.

findings.element: SectionCard tooltip trigger icon (passed via tooltip prop)
findings.description: The icon colour is compliant at 6.86:1 in light mode, but the dark-mode icon token Colors.dark.icon #94A3B8 on Colors.dark.surface #1E293B should be verified to confirm it meets the 3:1 non-text threshold.
findings.proposed_fix: Verify Colors.dark.icon (#94A3B8) on Colors.dark.surface (#1E293B): the ratio is approximately 2.4:1 — upgrade dark-mode icon colour to Colors.dark.textSecondary (#94A3B8 is already that token, so use Colors.dark.text #F1F5F9 at reduced opacity or a mid-slate #CBD5E1) to reach 3:1.

findings.element: Pressable secondaryButton — uses both styles.secondaryButton and styles.tightButton from static stylesheet
findings.description: Button background and text colours are entirely controlled by a static scheduler.styles file with no ThemeColors integration, creating a single-theme risk that will not adapt to system dark-mode switches.
findings.proposed_fix: Refactor secondaryButton and primaryButton style generators to accept a ThemeColors argument (e.g. makeStyles(colors: ThemeColors)) or use inline styles derived from useThemeColor so both light and dark surfaces are explicitly covered.

findings.description: The wrapper background is hardcoded to #0b5ad3 (a mid-blue) instead of a design-system token, bypassing the entire theming contract and rendering identically in both light and dark mode regardless of user preference.
findings.proposed_fix: Use brand.pro (#7C3AED) or brand.primaryDeep (#115E59) as the surface via a token: backgroundColor: colorScheme === 'dark' ? brand.proDark : brand.pro — or extract to a named surface token.

findings.element: bodyText — body copy on blue background
findings.description: #E5E7EB (Tailwind Gray-200, L≈0.791) on #0b5ad3 (L≈0.093) yields approximately 4.07:1, which fails WCAG AA for normal-weight body text (requires 4.5:1).
findings.proposed_fix: Replace color: '#E5E7EB' with color: '#FFFFFF' (white, ~7.1:1 on this background) or Colors.dark.text (#F1F5F9, ~7.0:1); update via token rather than hardcoded hex.

findings.element: secondaryText — 'Not now' label on semi-transparent white overlay
findings.description: The secondary button background is rgba(255,255,255,0.133) blended over #0b5ad3, producing an effective background of ~#2672d9; #E5E7EB on that surface is approximately 3.61:1, failing AA for normal text.
findings.proposed_fix: Change secondaryText color to '#FFFFFF' (white) which achieves ~5.5:1 on the blended surface, and set backgroundColor to 'rgba(255,255,255,0.18)' for a visible but accessible button shape.

findings.element: subtitle ThemedText — 'Time for a mindful pause' on blue background
findings.description: ThemedText with type='subtitle' resolves its color from the theme (light: #0F172A dark text on a blue card; dark: #F1F5F9 light text), but since the card background is hardcoded to #0b5ad3 regardless of theme, in light mode the dark text #0F172A achieves ~14:1 (fine), but if the device is in dark mode ThemedText emits #F1F5F9 which is only ~7.1:1 — this is acceptable, however the component never adapts its background so the subtitle colour contract is entirely accidental and unverifiable without knowing the resolved ThemedText colour at runtime.
findings.proposed_fix: Explicitly set subtitle text color to '#FFFFFF' via style prop on both ThemedText elements on this card, decoupled from the theme resolver, since the card background is always the same blue: <ThemedText type='subtitle' style={{ color: '#FFFFFF' }}>.

findings.description: Primary button uses hardcoded #ffffff background and #0b5ad3 text — ratio is acceptable (~7.1:1) but both colours bypass design tokens and will not adapt to future brand changes.
findings.proposed_fix: Use Colors.light.surface for background and a token such as brand.pro or brand.primaryDeep for the text label, e.g.: backgroundColor: Colors.light.surface, and primaryText color: brand.primaryDeep (#115E59, 5.87:1 on white).

findings.description: The card background is hardcoded to #0b5ad3 in StyleSheet.create, so it does not change in dark mode; ThemedText children will switch to dark-mode colours (lighter tones) against the same blue, causing unpredictable and untested contrast outcomes.
findings.proposed_fix: Detect color scheme with useColorScheme() and apply dynamic background: const bg = scheme === 'dark' ? brand.proDark : brand.pro; <ThemedView style={[styles.wrapper, { backgroundColor: bg }]}>

findings.description: Neither Pressable has a style function responding to pressed/focused state, so there is no visual feedback on press beyond the default ripple (Android only); on iOS there is zero pressed-state differentiation.
findings.proposed_fix: Use style={({ pressed }) => [styles.button, styles.primary, pressed && { opacity: 0.75 }]} on both buttons, or supply a distinct pressed background token.

findings.description: Both borderColor (#ffffff44, ~27% opacity) and backgroundColor (#ffffff22, ~13% opacity) are raw hex with alpha, hardcoded outside the token system; they will not adapt to theme or brand updates.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace with token-based semi-transparent values: backgroundColor: 'rgba(255,255,255,0.15)', borderColor: 'rgba(255,255,255,0.4)', or introduce a secondaryButtonBorder token in Colors.

findings.description: lineHeight is set to 20px but the default font size for body ThemedText is ~16px; 20/16 = 1.25× which is below the WCAG recommended 1.5× minimum (24px) for body text readability.
findings.proposed_fix: Increase to lineHeight: 24 (1.5× of 16px body size) to meet WCAG SC 1.4.12 text spacing guidance.

findings.description: shadowColor is hardcoded to #000000 — on dark backgrounds the black shadow is invisible and provides no elevation cue; a themed shadow colour would improve perceived depth in dark mode.
findings.proposed_fix: Use shadowColor: colorScheme === 'dark' ? '#000000' : '#1E293B' and ensure elevation is sufficient for dark surfaces.

findings.element: Touch target size — both Pressable buttons
findings.description: paddingVertical: 10 and paddingHorizontal: 14 yields an estimated touch target height of ~38px (10+18+10) for the label text, falling below the recommended 44px minimum for interactive elements.
findings.proposed_fix: Increase paddingVertical to 13 (yielding ~44px total) or add minHeight: 44 to the button style.

findings.description: Card background is hardcoded to #ffffff instead of using the Colors.light.surface token, meaning dark mode receives no override and will render white cards on the dark background, making content invisible.
findings.proposed_fix: Remove hardcoded backgroundColor from styles.card and apply it via a theme-aware hook: const colors = useThemeColors(); with backgroundColor: colors.surface in an inline or computed style.

findings.description: In dark mode the card still renders with a white (#ffffff) background while ThemedText renders light-coloured text (~#F1F5F9), producing near-zero contrast and making all card text illegible.
findings.proposed_fix: Use colors.surface (#1E293B in dark mode) as the card background via a dynamic style: backgroundColor: colors.surface.

findings.description: #6b7280 against white yields ~4.48:1, which falls just below the WCAG AA 4.5:1 threshold for normal-weight body text, making the summary a technical AA failure.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace color: '#6b7280' with color: colors.textSecondary which maps to #475569 (6.86:1 on white) in light mode and #94A3B8 (5.27:1) in dark mode — both pass AA.

findings.description: helperText colour is a hardcoded hex that never adapts; in dark mode the white card background keeps contrast marginally below AA, and if the card background were corrected to dark (#1E293B) the hardcoded #6b7280 would only achieve ~2.60:1 — a HIGH failure.
findings.proposed_fix: Use color: colors.textSecondary (token-driven) so the value resolves to #94A3B8 on dark backgrounds, achieving 5.27:1 on Colors.dark.surface.

findings.description: The container uses a hardcoded rgba-equivalent #ffffff11 which is semi-transparent; the effective background colour depends entirely on whatever surface sits behind it, making contrast unpredictable and unmaintainable — especially broken in dark mode where it barely lightens a dark background.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace backgroundColor: '#ffffff11' with backgroundColor: colors.surfaceRaised (or colors.surface with a border) so the background is opaque, token-driven, and theme-aware.

findings.description: The card border is hardcoded to #E5E7EB (Gray 200) which does not adapt to dark mode; in dark mode this light border on a corrected dark card surface would yield ~1.42:1, well below the 3:1 non-text UI component threshold.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace borderColor: '#E5E7EB' with borderColor: colors.border which resolves to #334155 in dark mode (sufficient contrast against #1E293B surface).

findings.description: The Pressable has no pressed, focused, or hovered visual feedback (no style callback, no ripple, no opacity change), meaning interactive state is invisible to sighted users and fails WCAG 2.4.11 Focus Appearance (AA in 2.2).
findings.proposed_fix: Use the style prop as a function: style={({ pressed }) => [styles.card, pressed && { backgroundColor: colors.background, borderColor: colors.borderFocus }]} and add accessibilityState where needed.

findings.description: The badge has bold fontWeight but no background colour or visual container to distinguish it as a badge/chip; it renders as plain text with no affordance, reducing its scannability despite adequate contrast.
findings.proposed_fix: Wrap the badge in a tinted surface, e.g. backgroundColor: colors.tint with color: '#FFFFFF', paddingHorizontal: 6, borderRadius: 10 to make the score visually distinct (tint #0D9488 gives 6.88:1 for white text).

findings.description: helperText has no explicit lineHeight set; React Native defaults to ~1.2× font-size, below the WCAG SC 1.4.8 / best-practice recommendation of ≥1.5× for readability of body/summary text.
findings.proposed_fix: Add lineHeight: 20 (for a default ~13–14px font) or lineHeight: 22 if fontSize is 14, achieving a 1.5× ratio. Alternatively reference a typography token if one exists.

findings.description: The title uses brand.primary (#0D9488) at 18px/700 weight on white; while bold 18px qualifies as large text (≥14pt bold), the ratio of 3.06:1 still fails the 3:1 AA Large threshold by a meaningful margin and is well below 4.5:1 for normal text.
findings.proposed_fix: Use Colors.light.text (#0F172A, 17.85:1) or brand.primaryDeep (#115E59, 5.87:1) for the title color: `color: brand.primaryDeep`

findings.description: At 12px, this text does not qualify as large text; however 6.86:1 does pass AA for normal text. But 12px is below the recommended 16px minimum body size, creating a readability failure under ambient-light conditions.
findings.proposed_fix: Increase fontSize to at minimum 14px (preferably 16px) to meet body text size best practices: `fontSize: 14`

findings.description: Contrast ratio itself passes AA, but 14px non-bold interactive button labels sit below the 44px minimum touch target height — paddingVertical:6 + fontSize:14 yields approximately 26px tap height, far below the 44px minimum.
findings.proposed_fix: Increase touch target: `paddingVertical: 14, paddingHorizontal: 12` to achieve ≥44px height for interactive buttons.

findings.description: The card's backgroundColor is hardcoded to Colors.light.surface (#FFFFFF) with no dark mode handling; in dark mode the card will render white on a dark backdrop with all text tokens also forced to light-mode values, causing incorrect dark-mode appearance and potential contrast inversions.
findings.proposed_fix: Accept a `colorScheme` prop or use a hook: `const colors = Colors[useColorScheme() ?? 'light']` and replace `Colors.light.surface` with `colors.surface`, and all other `Colors.light.*` references similarly.

findings.description: Colors.light.textSecondary is statically applied; in dark mode the card background will remain white (TS-004) but this text would still render at #475569 — if card is ever corrected to dark surface (#1E293B), #475569 achieves only approximately 2.5:1 against it, failing AA.
findings.proposed_fix: Resolve TS-004 first, then use `colors.textSecondary` dynamically so dark mode correctly applies #94A3B8 (5.27:1 on #1E293B).

findings.description: backgroundColor is set directly to Colors.light.surface rather than being resolved dynamically, locking the modal card to white in all color scheme contexts.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace `backgroundColor: Colors.light.surface` with a dynamic token resolved via `useColorScheme`: `backgroundColor: colors.surface`.

findings.description: White is hardcoded as a raw hex string rather than referencing a token; while the ratio passes AA (6.88:1), the hardcoded value bypasses the design system and will not adapt if the button background token changes.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace `color: '#FFFFFF'` with `color: Colors.light.surface` or define a semantic token `onPrimary: '#FFFFFF'` in the design system and reference it.

findings.description: The pressed background shift from #0D9488 to #0F766E is a very subtle darkening (only ~7% luminance change), which may be imperceptible to users with low contrast sensitivity or on bright outdoor displays; no visual scale, border, or opacity change supplements the color shift.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `opacity: 0.85` or `transform: [{ scale: 0.97 }]` alongside the color change, or use `brand.primaryDeep (#115E59)` for the pressed state to increase the color delta.

findings.description: The spotlight ring border is rgba(255,255,255,0.35), which at 35% opacity will fail the 3:1 non-text contrast requirement against most backgrounds and is effectively invisible on light-colored underlying UI.
findings.proposed_fix: Increase opacity to at least 0.7 or use a solid token color: `borderColor: 'rgba(255,255,255,0.75)'` to ensure the focus ring is perceivable as a UI boundary.

findings.description: shadowColor is a hardcoded raw hex '#000' rather than a design token; in dark mode a pure black shadow offers no separation from a dark backdrop.
findings.proposed_fix: For dark mode, use a lighter shadow or elevation-differentiated surface instead: resolve dynamically or remove shadow in dark mode, relying on `surfaceRaised` token for elevation cues.

findings.description: Contrast passes AA at 6.86:1 but body text at 14px with lineHeight 22 (1.57×) is acceptable; however 14px sits below the recommended 16px minimum for ambient-light mobile readability.
findings.proposed_fix: Increase description fontSize to 16px and keep lineHeight at 24 (1.5×): `fontSize: 16, lineHeight: 24`.

findings.element: Text buttons ('← Back', 'Skip tour') — no pressed state defined
findings.description: The textButton Pressable has no pressed style handler; there is no visual feedback on press, which fails best practice for interactive elements and may disorient users relying on visual state cues.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a pressed style callback: `style={({ pressed }) => [styles.textButton, pressed && { opacity: 0.5 }]}` for both Back and Skip tour buttons.

findings.description: 12px text is below WCAG's minimum 'normal text' baseline and is the smallest text in the component; even though ratio passes AA numerically, 12px is an ambient-light readability risk especially on lower-DPI screens.
findings.proposed_fix: Increase stepCounter fontSize to at least 14px: `fontSize: 14`, and consider using Colors.light.textTertiary only if size is raised to 14px+ where 4.35:1 is sufficient.

findings.description: styles.mutedText resolved to textTertiary (#64748B, 4.35:1) falls below the 4.5:1 AA threshold for normal-weight body text displaying role and time-range information — this is informational text, not a placeholder, so the placeholder exemption does not apply.
findings.proposed_fix: Apply Colors.light.textSecondary (#475569, 6.86:1) for this informational line; update schedulerStyles.mutedText to use textSecondary token.

findings.element: secondaryButton label — 'Auto Assign' button text using primaryButtonText style on secondaryButton background
findings.background: styles.secondaryButton — unknown background, likely brand.primary #0D9488 or a light teal surface
findings.description: The Auto Assign Pressable uses styles.secondaryButton for its container but styles.primaryButtonText for its label; if secondaryButton is a light teal or white-background outlined variant, white text on it will fail contrast, and if it is a filled teal it may only achieve ~3.06:1 — the mismatch between button style and text style is a likely AA failure.
findings.proposed_fix: Ensure secondaryButton text uses the correct token: white text (#FFFFFF) only when background is brand.primaryDark (#0F766E, 9.30:1) or deeper; for a light/outlined secondary button use Colors.light.text (#0F172A) or brand.primaryDeep (#115E59, 5.87:1) as the label colour and update to a dedicated styles.secondaryButtonText token.

findings.element: mutedText inside auto-assign suggestion list rendered inside ThemedView bannerSuccess
findings.background: styles.bannerSuccess — likely Colors.light.successSurface #ECFDF5 in light / Colors.dark.successSurface #064E3B in dark
findings.description: In dark mode, textTertiary #64748B on successSurface #064E3B (very dark green) produces an extremely low contrast ratio — #64748B against #064E3B is estimated at approximately 2.1:1, a clear WCAG AA failure for normal text.
findings.proposed_fix: Inside the bannerSuccess ThemedView, override mutedText colour to Colors.dark.textSecondary (#94A3B8, ~5.27:1 on #064E3B) or Colors.dark.text (#F1F5F9) via a conditional style driven by useColorScheme.

findings.element: Apply / Applying button text (primaryButtonText) when autoAssignApplying disabled state applied
