findings.background: styles.disabledButton — unknown, likely a washed-out teal or grey such as #94A3B8 or similar low-luminance muted tone
findings.description: When autoAssignApplying is true the disabledButton style is merged; if the disabled background is a mid-grey or desaturated teal, white text may drop below 4.5:1, and the visual change must also be detectable as a state change (see STS-008).
findings.proposed_fix: Define disabledButton background as #CBD5E1 (Slate 300) and pair with dark text Colors.light.text (#0F172A, ~13:1) rather than white, ensuring both contrast compliance and visible disabled state.

findings.element: ghostEmptyCtaText and ghostEmptyNote in empty-state ghost container
findings.foreground: styles.ghostEmptyCtaText / ghostEmptyNote — token unknown, likely textTertiary
findings.background: styles.ghostContainer / ghostEmptyCta — likely surface #FFFFFF light / #1E293B dark
findings.description: Ghost empty-state copy uses muted text tokens that may be themed inconsistently across modes; in dark mode textTertiary #64748B on surface #1E293B yields approximately 3.6:1, failing AA for normal text.
findings.proposed_fix: Use textSecondary token (Colors.[scheme].textSecondary) for ghost CTA and note text to guarantee ≥4.5:1 in both modes; reserve textTertiary only for decorative placeholder-exempt content.

findings.description: If successText uses the brand.success token (#10B981, 2.88:1 on white) rather than the corrected Colors.light.success (#15803D), it fails in light mode; even if corrected to #15803D, the dark-mode equivalent must use Colors.dark.success (#34D399) which needs verification against the dark surface.
findings.proposed_fix: Explicitly bind successText foreground to Colors.light.success (#15803D) in light and Colors.dark.success (#34D399) in dark via useColorScheme; #34D399 on #1E293B yields approximately 7.5:1 ✅.

findings.description: Light mode correctly uses #DC2626 (4.64:1); dark mode must use Colors.dark.error (#F87171) — if errorText is a static hardcoded colour it will not adapt and #DC2626 on #1E293B is approximately 3.9:1, failing AA.
findings.proposed_fix: Drive errorText colour through the theme token: Colors.light.error in light mode, Colors.dark.error (#F87171) in dark mode, using useColorScheme or a ThemedText type variant.

findings.element: Apply button disabled state when autoAssignApplying=true
findings.description: The disabled state is applied only via a conditional style merge with no accessibilityState={{ disabled: true }} prop, and the visual differentiation between enabled and disabled relies entirely on whatever opacity or colour change disabledButton provides — without explicit disabled accessibilityState, screen readers will not announce the button as unavailable.
findings.proposed_fix: Add accessibilityState={{ disabled: autoAssignApplying }} to the Pressable; ensure disabledButton reduces opacity to ≤0.4 or changes background sufficiently (≥3:1 distinguishable from enabled state) to meet WCAG 1.4.11 non-text contrast for the state boundary.

findings.element: Time placeholders '09:00' and '17:00' in start/end InputField
findings.foreground: InputField placeholder colour — likely textTertiary #64748B or old #94A3B8
findings.description: If InputField's placeholder colour inherits the deprecated #94A3B8 token it sits exactly at 3.0:1, the WCAG 2.1 minimum for placeholder-exempt text, leaving no ambient-light safety margin for outdoor mobile use.
findings.proposed_fix: Ensure InputField uses at minimum textTertiary #64748B (4.35:1) for placeholder colour; this also future-proofs against WCAG 2.2 draft guidance that may remove the placeholder exemption.

findings.element: Ghost skeleton blocks (ghostNameBar, ghostTimeBar, ghostBadgeBar) — decorative loading shimmer
findings.foreground: styles.ghostNameBar etc — colour unknown, likely a light grey
findings.description: Ghost/skeleton placeholder bars are marked accessibilityElementsHidden, so they are exempt from text contrast rules, but if their fill colour is too close to the container background they become invisible in high-ambient-light conditions and lose their communicative purpose as loading indicators.
findings.proposed_fix: Use a ghost fill of at minimum Colors.light.border (#E2E8F0) on white surface; verify ≥1.5:1 decorative threshold or add a subtle shimmer animation to maintain perceptual separation without requiring full 3:1 compliance.

findings.description: The '?' character is rendered at 16px normal weight using brand.primary (#0D9488) on a white/surface background, achieving only 3.06:1 which fails WCAG AA for normal-size text.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace `color: brand.primary` with `color: Colors[colorScheme ?? 'light'].tint` is still #0D9488 in light mode — instead use `brand.primaryDeep` (#115E59, 5.87:1) or `brand.primaryDark` (#0F766E, 4.01:1 — still marginal); safest fix: use `Colors[colorScheme ?? 'light'].text` (#0F172A) or a dedicated token. In dark mode use Colors.dark.tint (#2DD4BF, 8.95:1 vs dark background).

findings.element: TourTriggerButton '?' label text in dark mode
findings.description: In dark mode the '?' text color is still hardcoded to brand.primary (#0D9488) but the background becomes Colors.dark.surface (#1E293B), yielding approximately 2.44:1 — a severe AA failure for normal body text.
findings.proposed_fix: Remove the hardcoded `color: brand.primary` from the ThemedText style and instead derive the color from the color scheme: use `Colors[colorScheme ?? 'light'].tint` which resolves to #2DD4BF in dark mode (8.95:1 vs #1E293B) and apply the same fix noted in TLY-001 for light mode.

findings.element: SignOutButton IconSymbol icon in light mode
findings.description: The sign-out icon uses Colors.light.tint (#0D9488) which achieves exactly 3.06:1 — it technically passes the 3:1 non-text minimum but provides zero safety margin; on slightly off-white header backgrounds or in bright ambient light it will effectively fail visibility.
findings.proposed_fix: Use `brand.primaryDark` (#0F766E, 4.01:1) or `brand.primaryDeep` (#115E59, 5.87:1) as the icon color in light mode to provide a meaningful safety margin above 3:1. Token expression: `Colors[colorScheme ?? 'light'].tint` already uses the correct dark-mode value (#2DD4BF) — only the light-mode tint token itself needs to be updated or overridden locally.

findings.description: The color is hardcoded to `brand.primary` rather than a theme-aware token, so it does not adapt to dark mode, bypassing the design token system.
findings.proposed_fix: Remove the inline `color: brand.primary` property from the ThemedText style entirely and let ThemedText use its default `Colors[scheme].text` token, or pass a scheme-aware color: `color: Colors[colorScheme ?? 'light'].tint` (but also fix TLY-001 for the light-mode ratio).

findings.foreground: brand.primary + '22' (#0D948822 — ~13% opacity teal) pressed / transparent unpressed
findings.description: The unpressed state is fully transparent (surface + '00') and the pressed state applies only a 13% opacity tint (#0D948822), making the pressed affordance nearly imperceptible — there is no visual distinction between idle and active states sufficient to meet WCAG 1.4.11 non-text contrast for interactive component states.
findings.proposed_fix: Increase pressed background opacity to at least 30–40% (e.g., `brand.primary + '55'` ≈ 33% opacity) and consider adding an unpressed subtle border or background: `backgroundColor: Colors[colorScheme ?? 'light'].border` at rest, transitioning to `brand.primarySurface` (#F0FDFA) on press, giving a clear state change above 3:1.

findings.description: In dark mode, tabIconDefault is #64748B (Slate 500) against the dark background #0F172A, yielding approximately 3.04:1 — only just above the 3:1 non-text minimum with no safety margin, and tab labels at 12–14px require 4.5:1 as normal-size text.
findings.proposed_fix: Override `tabBarInactiveTintColor` in screenOptions to use `Colors[colorScheme ?? 'light'].textSecondary` which in dark mode resolves to #94A3B8 (5.27:1 vs #0F172A), providing adequate contrast for both icon and label text.

findings.description: The button is sized at 28×28px, which is below the WCAG 2.5.5 recommended minimum touch target of 44×44px, making it difficult to tap accurately for users with motor impairments.
findings.proposed_fix: Increase `width` and `height` to 44 and `borderRadius` to 22, or keep the visual size at 28×28 but add `hitSlop={{ top: 8, bottom: 8, left: 8, right: 8 }}` to expand the interactive area to 44×44 without affecting layout.

findings.description: The '?' text has fontSize 16 and lineHeight 20 (1.25× ratio), below the WCAG 1.4.8 and general best-practice recommendation of ≥1.5× line-height (24px) for body text.
findings.proposed_fix: Update to `lineHeight: 24` (1.5× of fontSize 16) — though for a single-character button label this is less critical, aligning with the design system's typography standards is recommended.

findings.description: SignOutButton uses paddingHorizontal 14 and paddingVertical 8; with the icon at 22px the total height is approximately 38px (22 + 16), falling short of the 44px minimum touch target height.
findings.proposed_fix: Increase `paddingVertical` from 8 to 11 to bring the total tappable height to 44px, or add `minHeight: 44` to the style object.

findings.description: The hardcoded hex #0a7ea4 on a white/light surface achieves only ~4.07:1, failing WCAG AA for normal-sized (16px) body text and bypassing the design token system entirely.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace `color: '#0a7ea4'` in styles.link with a dynamic token — use `Colors.light.primaryDeep` (#115E59, 5.87:1) for light mode and `Colors.dark.tint` (#2DD4BF, 8.95:1) for dark mode, applied via `useThemeColor` just like the main `color` resolution, e.g. add a `linkColor = useThemeColor({}, 'tint')` call and apply it conditionally when `type === 'link'`.

findings.element: link type text in dark mode
findings.description: The hardcoded link colour #0a7ea4 is not overridden in dark mode; against the dark background #0F172A it collapses to ~2.91:1, a clear AA failure for 16px text.
findings.proposed_fix: Remove the hardcoded `color` from `styles.link` entirely and resolve it through `useThemeColor({ light: Colors.light.primaryDeep, dark: Colors.dark.tint }, 'tint')` so both modes receive a passing token value.

findings.element: subtitle type text in dark mode (textTertiary fallback risk)
findings.description: If a consumer passes `darkColor` resolving to `textTertiary` (#64748B) for a subtitle, contrast against the dark background #0F172A is only ~2.74:1; additionally the dark `tabIconDefault` / `textTertiary` token itself is only safe in light mode — the audit flag documents that using dark.textTertiary (#64748B) on dark.background is a HIGH failure path enabled by this component's unconstrained `darkColor` prop.
findings.proposed_fix: Document (via TypeScript or a runtime warning in dev) that `darkColor` must not be set to `Colors.dark.textTertiary`; enforce a minimum by defaulting dark text resolution to `Colors.dark.text` (#F1F5F9) or `Colors.dark.textSecondary` (#94A3B8, 5.27:1) rather than allowing callers to pass unchecked values.

findings.element: title type text — lineHeight equals fontSize
findings.description: Contrast for title text is excellent, but lineHeight: 32 equals fontSize: 32 (ratio 1.0×), providing zero leading between wrapped title lines, which severely harms readability for users with cognitive or low-vision needs even though the colour contrast passes.
findings.proposed_fix: Set `lineHeight: 40` (1.25× of 32px) as a minimum; for accessibility-sensitive copy prefer `lineHeight: 48` (1.5×) — e.g. `lineHeight: 40` in styles.title.

findings.description: The subtitle style (20px bold) has no lineHeight defined, so React Native falls back to a platform default (~1.2×), which is below the WCAG recommended 1.5× for body-adjacent text and reduces readability on wrapped lines.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `lineHeight: 30` (1.5× of 20px) to `styles.subtitle`.

findings.element: link style — colour not composable with theme overrides
findings.description: Because `styles.link` sets `color` inside a static StyleSheet, it will always win over the `{ color }` entry in the style array unless a caller explicitly overrides it, making the token-driven colour from `useThemeColor` silently ineffective for link-type text.
findings.proposed_fix: Move link colour out of the static StyleSheet into the inline style array: apply it as `type === 'link' ? { color: linkColor } : undefined` where `linkColor` is resolved via `useThemeColor`, ensuring token precedence is correct.

findings.description: lineHeight: 24 on fontSize: 16 gives a 1.5× ratio which meets WCAG SC 1.4.8 recommendation; this is correct and noted as a positive, but ambient-light / outdoor mobile use benefits from the slightly larger 1.6× (26px) recommended by APCA for small screens.
findings.proposed_fix: Consider increasing lineHeight to 26 for default and defaultSemiBold to improve readability in bright outdoor conditions — low priority but beneficial for the stated use-case.

findings.element: link type text — no pressed / visited state differentiation
findings.description: The link style provides no visual affordance for pressed, focused, or visited states beyond the base colour, meaning interactive state changes are invisible to keyboard and switch-access users.
findings.proposed_fix: Wrap link-type rendering in a Pressable with `onPressIn`/`onPressOut` state, applying `textDecorationLine: 'underline'` on focus/hover and a colour shift to `Colors.light.primaryDeep` (#115E59) on press to provide a non-colour state cue.

findings.description: brand.primary (#0D9488) renders at 16px non-bold which is normal text size, achieving only 3.06:1 against light backgrounds — fails WCAG AA normal text (4.5:1 required).
findings.proposed_fix: Change iconText color to Colors.light.tint resolved via useColorScheme: use 'brand.primaryDeep' (#115E59, 5.87:1) in light mode and 'Colors.dark.tint' (#2DD4BF, 8.95:1) in dark mode; e.g. color: colorScheme === 'dark' ? '#2DD4BF' : '#115E59'.

findings.description: The tooltip card background is hardcoded as '#1C2B3A', bypassing the design token system entirely and making it impossible to adapt to light/dark mode or future theme changes.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace with a token: use Colors.dark.surface (#1E293B) as a constant dark card color, or better, drive it from useColorScheme — e.g. backgroundColor: colorScheme === 'dark' ? Colors.dark.surfaceRaised : Colors.dark.surface — keeping it intentionally dark for overlay contrast in both modes.

findings.description: #E8F4F1 is a non-token hex; while it visually resembles a light slate, its exact contrast against the non-token card background #1C2B3A cannot be verified against the design system and may drift if either value changes.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace with Colors.dark.text (#F1F5F9), which is a verified token with 15.65:1 against #0F172A and provides safe contrast against any dark surface in the system; e.g. color: Colors.dark.text.

findings.description: White text on brand.primary (#0D9488) achieves 6.88:1 which passes AA for normal text — this finding is a correction: the ratio is acceptable. However the color is hardcoded '#fff' instead of using a token.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace hardcoded '#fff' with the token Colors.light.surface or a semantic 'onPrimary' white constant to keep it within the token system; the contrast ratio itself is compliant at 6.88:1.

findings.description: The pressed-state background uses brand.primary at ~13% opacity (#0D948822); on a dark background (#0F172A) this near-transparent teal is virtually invisible, providing no perceptible pressed feedback in dark mode.
findings.proposed_fix: Use a higher-opacity token-based overlay in dark mode: e.g. Colors.dark.tint + '33' (#2DD4BF33, ~20% opacity) which provides a visible teal tint against the dark surface, toggled via useColorScheme.

findings.description: brand.primary (#0D9488) is a mid-teal that was chosen for light mode; against the dark background #0F172A its luminance difference is insufficient — estimated ~2.5:1 — failing AA for the 16px non-bold ⓘ glyph in dark mode.
findings.proposed_fix: Conditionally apply Colors.dark.tint (#2DD4BF) in dark mode, which achieves 8.95:1 against the dark background; use useColorScheme to switch: color: colorScheme === 'dark' ? Colors.dark.tint : brand.primaryDeep.

findings.element: Native modal: full-screen Pressable dismiss area has no backdrop tint
findings.description: The native dismiss area uses StyleSheet.absoluteFill with no background color, meaning the tooltip card floats over the live page with no scrim — users receive no visual signal that a modal layer is active, and the card may have insufficient contrast against complex underlying content.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a semi-transparent backdrop to the dismiss Pressable: backgroundColor: 'rgba(15,23,42,0.45)' (using Slate 900 at 45% opacity) to create a legible scrim that separates the modal layer from page content.

findings.description: shadowColor is hardcoded '#000'; while shadow colors are not subject to contrast requirements, this bypasses the token system and the shadow at 0.3 opacity on a near-black card (#1C2B3A) in light mode may be invisible, reducing perceived card elevation.
findings.proposed_fix: Use shadowColor: Colors.light.text (#0F172A) or simply '#000000' kept as a documented constant; more importantly ensure shadowOpacity is increased to 0.45 in light mode for perceptible card separation from light backgrounds.

findings.description: The Pressable trigger has no explicit focus-visible outline or ring style for keyboard/switch-access users; on web, browser default outlines may be suppressed by React Native Web's reset styles.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a platform-conditional outlineWidth / outlineColor style on focus: e.g. Platform.OS === 'web' && focused && { outline: '2px solid #0D9488', outlineOffset: 2 } using a focusable state variable via onFocus/onBlur, referencing Colors.light.borderFocus (#0D9488).

findings.description: 14px (10.5pt) is below the 16px recommended minimum body size for comfortable reading on mobile; while the contrast may be sufficient, the small size combined with a non-system font rendering in a modal overlay increases legibility risk on low-DPI screens.
findings.proposed_fix: Increase tooltipText fontSize to 15 or 16 and set lineHeight to 24 (1.5× of 16px) to satisfy the WCAG 1.4.12 text spacing guidance and improve ambient-light readability.

findings.element: 'Got it ✓' closeButton — no pressed state style
findings.description: The closeButton Pressable has no pressed/hovered visual state; users receive no tactile feedback that the button is interactive, which is a best-practice gap especially on web where hover indication is expected.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a pressed style using brand.primaryDark (#0F766E) as the pressed backgroundColor: style={({ pressed }) => [styles.closeButton, pressed && { backgroundColor: brand.primaryDark }]}. White text on #0F766E achieves 9.30:1 — fully AAA compliant.

findings.description: The message text uses a hardcoded hex #475569 (Colors.light.textSecondary) which is correct in light mode but completely ignores the dark-mode surface, where this slate-600 value yields roughly 2.27:1 against #0F172A — a hard WCAG AA failure.
findings.proposed_fix: Remove the hardcoded `color` from styles.message and rely on ThemedText's inherited themed colour (Colors.light.textSecondary / Colors.dark.textSecondary via the ThemedText component), or pass `type='secondary'` if ThemedText supports it.

findings.description: The button background #2563EB (Blue 600) is a raw hardcoded hex that is not part of the Horario design token system; white text on #2563EB yields ~5.9:1 which passes AA in isolation, but the colour is inconsistent with the teal brand primary and will not adapt to any future token changes or theming.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace `backgroundColor: '#2563EB'` with the design token `brand.primaryDark` (#0F766E) or `brand.primary` (#0D9488) — white text on primaryDark yields 9.30:1 (AAA) and keeps brand consistency.

findings.description: buttonText hardcodes `color: '#FFFFFF'`; while white-on-blue passes AA, both the foreground and background bypass the token system entirely, creating a combined risk if either value is ever adjusted in isolation without checking the pair.
findings.proposed_fix: Use a token-derived value: set `color: Colors.light.surface` (resolves to #FFFFFF) and pair it with the token-backed button background from EB-002 fix; or extract to a shared ButtonPrimary component that manages both colours atomically.

findings.description: Even if EB-001 is classified as a hardcoded-colour issue, the functional consequence in dark mode is a separate critical gap: #475569 on #0F172A is approximately 2.27:1, well below AA for the 14 px body text used here.
findings.proposed_fix: Adopt ThemedText without an overriding color style so the component automatically applies Colors.dark.textSecondary (#94A3B8, 5.27:1 on #0F172A) in dark mode.

findings.element: Retry button — dark mode surface adaptation
findings.description: The button uses a static StyleSheet with no dark-mode variant; on a dark background (#0F172A / #1E293B) a blue-600 button may blend poorly with surrounding dark surfaces and lacks the elevated-contrast treatment recommended for primary actions in dark environments.
findings.proposed_fix: Use a dynamic style via `useColorScheme` and apply `brand.primaryDark` (#0F766E) in light and `brand.primary` (#0D9488) in dark (teal 400 `#2DD4BF` is the dark tint token if a lighter feel is preferred), ensuring the button remains visually salient against dark surfaces.

findings.element: Pressable Retry button — pressed / disabled states
findings.description: The Pressable has no `style` function to communicate pressed feedback (e.g. opacity or background shift), meaning the pressed state is visually indistinguishable from the resting state on devices where the default ripple is not visible (iOS / older Android).
findings.proposed_fix: Change `style={styles.button}` to `style={({ pressed }) => [styles.button, pressed && styles.buttonPressed]}` and add `buttonPressed: { opacity: 0.75 }` (or a darker background token) to StyleSheet to provide clear pressed feedback.

findings.description: The message text is set at fontSize 14 with lineHeight 20 (ratio 1.43×); WCAG and typography best-practice recommend a minimum line-height of 1.5× the font size for body text, meaning lineHeight should be at least 21 for 14 px text.
findings.proposed_fix: Update styles.message to `lineHeight: 22` (1.57× of 14) to meet the ≥1.5× guideline and improve readability for users with cognitive or low-vision needs.

findings.element: Pressable Retry button touch target height
findings.description: With paddingVertical 10 and a typical ThemedText line-height of ~20 px, the effective touch target is approximately 40 px tall, below the WCAG 2.5.5 / Apple HIG recommended minimum of 44 px.
findings.proposed_fix: Increase `paddingVertical` to at least 12–14 to bring the total tappable height to ≥44 px, or add `minHeight: 44` to styles.button.

findings.description: The comment '// was #9CA3AF 2.54:1 FAIL' documents a previously used value that fails AA — retaining it in code risks a future developer reverting to it; the deprecated value should be removed from the codebase entirely.
findings.proposed_fix: Delete the inline comment referencing #9CA3AF and instead reference the token name in a brief comment: `// Colors.light.textSecondary — 6.86:1 ✓ AA` to make the intent clear without preserving the failing value.

findings.foreground: styles.badgeText (unknown hex — likely white #FFFFFF or brand.accent #F59E0B)
findings.background: styles.positiveBadge (unknown hex — likely brand.success #10B981 or brand.accent #F59E0B)
findings.description: The badge text colour applied via styles.badgeText against the positiveBadge background is not token-auditable from this file; common choices like white-on-Emerald-500 (#10B981) yield only 2.88:1 or amber-on-white yield 2.08:1, both failing WCAG AA for normal text.
findings.proposed_fix: Ensure badgeText uses Colors.light.text (#0F172A) or Colors.light.surface (#FFFFFF) only against a background that achieves ≥4.5:1; for a green positive badge use background #15803D (Green 700) with white text (5.44:1 ✓ AA), matching Colors.light.success.

findings.element: Badge text (deltaLabel) on default/negative badge background
findings.background: styles.badge (unknown hex — likely brand.error #EF4444 or brand.accent #F59E0B)
findings.description: When metrics.delta < 0 the component falls back to styles.badge for both wrapper and badge styling; if the badge background uses brand.error (#EF4444) with white text the ratio is only 4.55:1 which is borderline, and if it uses brand.accent (#F59E0B) it collapses to 2.08:1 — a hard WCAG AA failure.
findings.proposed_fix: Use Colors.light.error (#DC2626, 4.64:1 ✓ AA) as the negative badge background with white text (#FFFFFF), or Colors.light.warning (#B45309, 4.82:1 ✓ AA) for amber-toned negative states. Never use brand.accent (#F59E0B) as a text-bearing background on white or light surfaces.

findings.element: Progress fill bar against progress track
findings.background: styles.progressTrack background colour (unknown — likely Colors.light.border #E2E8F0 or brand.primarySurface #F0FDFA)
findings.description: A progress bar is a non-text UI component requiring 3:1 contrast between the fill and its track; if brand.primary (#0D9488) is used on border (#E2E8F0) the ratio is approximately 2.7:1, failing WCAG 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast.
findings.proposed_fix: Use Colors.light.primaryDark (#0F766E) for the fill — it achieves ~3.5:1 against #E2E8F0 — or use Colors.light.primaryDeep (#115E59) for a comfortable 4:1+ against the track.

findings.element: Muted descriptive body text (styles.mutedText) — 'Estimated revenue at risk…'
findings.description: This is informational body text (not a placeholder), so the WCAG placeholder exemption does not apply; rendering it in textTertiary (#64748B) on the off-white page background (#F8FAFC) drops the ratio below the 4.5:1 AA threshold for normal-weight text.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace styles.mutedText foreground with Colors.light.textSecondary (#475569, 6.86:1 on white / ~6.6:1 on #F8FAFC ✓ AA) for all non-placeholder descriptive text.

findings.element: positiveBadge and badge styles — colour not defined per theme
findings.description: The badge background and text colours appear to be hardcoded in scheduler.styles without dark-mode variants, meaning the same surface colour will render against Colors.dark.surface (#1E293B) in dark mode, likely producing an invisible or failing badge.
findings.proposed_fix: In scheduler.styles, drive badge colours through the theme hook: positive badge → { backgroundColor: Colors.dark.successSurface (#064E3B), color: Colors.dark.success (#34D399) }; negative badge → { backgroundColor: Colors.dark.errorSurface (#450A0A), color: Colors.dark.error (#F87171) }.

findings.element: Progress track and fill in dark mode
findings.description: If progressTrack uses a light-mode border colour (e.g. #E2E8F0) without a dark-mode override, it will be barely visible against Colors.dark.surface (#1E293B), and any fill using a teal that works on light surfaces may blend into the dark background.
findings.proposed_fix: Set progressTrack background to Colors.dark.border (#334155) and progressFill to Colors.dark.tint (#2DD4BF) in dark mode — #2DD4BF on #334155 yields approximately 5.1:1 ✓ AA for the non-text component boundary.

findings.element: Negative badge — style falls back to styles.badge instead of a dedicated negativeBadge
findings.description: When metrics.delta < 0 the ternary applies styles.badge twice (no negativeBadge style), so positive and negative states are visually indistinguishable beyond the deltaLabel sign character alone.
findings.proposed_fix: Define a styles.negativeBadge with backgroundColor: Colors.light.errorSurface (#FEF2F2) and a text colour of Colors.light.error (#DC2626, 4.64:1 ✓ AA), and apply it in the ternary: metrics.delta >= 0 ? styles.positiveBadge : styles.negativeBadge.

findings.element: Inline style alignItems on 'After forecast' column wrapper
findings.description: The inline style={{ alignItems: 'flex-end' }} is not a colour issue, but the pattern of inline styles alongside stylesheet-driven theme tokens risks future authors adding hardcoded colour values here without design-system review.
findings.proposed_fix: Extract to schedulerStyles as styles.columnRight: { alignItems: 'flex-end' } to keep all visual declarations in the auditable stylesheet.

findings.description: styles.mutedText maps to Colors.light.textTertiary (#64748B, Slate 500). At 4.35:1 this fails WCAG AA for normal-weight body text (< 18px / < 14px bold). The subtitle and step description strings rendered here are informational content, not placeholders, so the placeholder exemption does not apply.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace the foreground color with Colors.light.textSecondary (#475569, Slate 600, 6.86:1) for all non-placeholder informational text, or darken textTertiary to #5E6E82 (≥ 4.5:1) and use that token exclusively for labelled-field placeholders.

findings.description: Teal 600 (#0D9488) used as badge background with white (#FFFFFF) text yields approximately 3.24:1, failing WCAG AA for normal text. Progress percentage is small informational text likely rendered below 18px regular weight.
findings.proposed_fix: Switch badge background to Colors.light.primaryDeep (#115E59, Teal 800). White on #115E59 achieves ~5.8:1, passing AA. Alternatively use Colors.light.text (#0F172A) as foreground on the current teal background (4.72:1, passes AA).

findings.description: Incomplete step indicators likely use textTertiary (#64748B) or a mid-gray as the circle background with white numeral text. #FFFFFF on #64748B is approximately 3.69:1, failing WCAG AA for normal text. Even if the circle is 24px, numerals inside are typically rendered at 12–14px normal weight.
findings.proposed_fix: Darken the incomplete indicator background to at least #475569 (Slate 600). White on #475569 is ~6.86:1 (AAA). Alternatively use Colors.light.primaryDark (#0F766E) background with white text (~4.6:1, passes AA).

findings.description: styles.linkText likely applies Colors.light.tint / brand.primary (#0D9488) as foreground on the white card surface. Teal 600 on white achieves only ~3.24:1, which fails AA for normal-weight text links that are not at least 18px or 14px bold.
findings.proposed_fix: Use Colors.light.primaryDark (#0F766E, Teal 700) which achieves ~4.6:1 on white, or Colors.light.primaryDeep (#115E59, Teal 800) at ~5.8:1. Apply underline decoration to reinforce link affordance without relying solely on color.

findings.description: In dark mode, Colors.dark.textTertiary (#64748B, Slate 500) on the surface color (#1E293B, Slate 800) yields approximately 2.10:1. This critically fails WCAG AA. The same mutedText style is reused for subtitle and step descriptions, both of which are informational body text.
findings.proposed_fix: For dark mode, map mutedText to Colors.dark.textSecondary (#94A3B8, Slate 400). #94A3B8 on #1E293B achieves approximately 4.6:1, passing AA. Ensure ThemedText resolves the correct dark-mode token rather than a hardcoded hex.

findings.description: If the progress badge background remains brand.primary (#0D9488) in dark mode and the text resolves to Colors.dark.text (#F1F5F9), the ratio is approximately 3.38:1, still failing AA for small normal-weight text.
findings.proposed_fix: In dark mode use Colors.dark.tint (#2DD4BF, Teal 400) as badge background only if paired with a dark foreground (#0F172A), yielding ~10.5:1. Alternatively keep a dark badge background (#115E59) with light text (#F1F5F9) at ~6.1:1.

findings.description: The unfilled track of the progress bar (likely Colors.light.border, #E2E8F0) against the white card surface (#FFFFFF) achieves only ~1.37:1. WCAG 1.4.11 requires UI component boundaries to meet 3:1. The track is a meaningful UI component indicating overall progress.
findings.proposed_fix: Use #CBD5E1 (Slate 300, ~2.3:1) or #94A3B8 (Slate 400, ~4.6:1) for the track background to meet the 3:1 non-text contrast requirement for the visible track boundary.

findings.description: If the step indicator circle for incomplete steps is rendered as an outlined circle using the border color (#E2E8F0) on the white card, the boundary contrast is ~1.37:1, failing WCAG 1.4.11 non-text contrast at 3:1. Users with low vision may not perceive the circle boundary.
findings.proposed_fix: Use at least #94A3B8 (Slate 400, 4.6:1 on white) for the indicator border or fill the incomplete indicator with a mid-gray background (e.g., #CBD5E1) so the shape boundary meets 3:1 against the card surface.

findings.description: The hardcoded placeholder colour #9CA3AF (Gray 400) achieves only ~2.85:1 on a white surface, falling below even the WCAG 2.1 placeholder minimum of 3:1, and completely bypasses the design token system.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace `placeholderTextColor="#9CA3AF"` with a themed token: use `Colors[colorScheme].textTertiary` (#64748B in light = 4.35:1, #64748B in dark ≈ 2.55:1 — see IF-002) or at minimum `'#6B7280'` (Gray 500, ~4.05:1 on white). Consume via `useColorScheme` and the Colors token map.

findings.description: The hardcoded #9CA3AF is never adjusted for dark mode; against the dark surface (#1E293B) it drops to approximately 2.41:1, failing the 3:1 WCAG placeholder minimum in both modes but critically so in dark mode.
findings.proposed_fix: Derive placeholderTextColor from the active color scheme: `const placeholderColor = colorScheme === 'dark' ? '#94A3B8' : '#64748B';` — #94A3B8 on #1E293B ≈ 3.64:1 (passes 3:1) and #64748B on #FFFFFF = 4.35:1. Wire via `useColorScheme()` inside a wrapper or pass as a prop from the themed parent.

findings.element: TextInput (styles.input) — background and text colour in dark mode
findings.description: The TextInput uses `style={styles.input}` from a static StyleSheet (scheduler.styles) with no apparent dark-mode branching visible in this file; if the stylesheet hardcodes a light background/text pair, the input will be invisible or low-contrast in dark mode.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace the static `styles.input` background/color values with tokens from `Colors[colorScheme]`: surface for background, text for color, and border for borderColor — consumed via `useColorScheme()` and merged as an inline style override or a themed stylesheet factory.

findings.element: ThemedText label (styles.label) — colour in dark mode
findings.description: ThemedText should self-theme its colour, but `styles.label` from the static scheduler stylesheet may override the themed colour with a hardcoded light-mode value, breaking dark mode legibility for the field label.
findings.proposed_fix: Remove any `color` or `fontSize` overrides from `styles.label` that could clobber ThemedText's internal theming, or ensure styles.label is produced by a dark-mode-aware factory that reads `Colors[colorScheme].text` for the label colour.

findings.description: The TextInput lacks an explicit `accessibilityRole` (should be 'none' or omitted only if the OS default is reliably 'text'), and the placeholder string is used as visible hint content without a complementary `accessibilityHint` fallback, reducing screen-reader context when placeholder is absent.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `accessibilityRole="none"` (RN default for TextInput is correct but explicit is safer) and ensure that when `placeholder` carries semantic meaning it is also surfaced via `accessibilityHint={accessibilityHint ?? placeholder}` so VoiceOver/TalkBack users receive equivalent guidance.

findings.description: styles.mutedText is an external token whose resolved colour is not visible in this file; if it resolves to the deprecated #94A3B8 (old textTertiary, 3.0:1 on white) it fails WCAG AA for normal body text, and any badge background darker or tinted than white will reduce the ratio further.
findings.proposed_fix: Ensure styles.mutedText maps to Colors.light.textSecondary (#475569, 6.86:1) for informational time text; never use the deprecated #94A3B8 or Colors.dark.textTertiary (#64748B, 4.35:1) as a muted colour on coloured badge surfaces.

findings.foreground: unknown (styles.badgeText — possibly brand.primary #0D9488 or a light-on-teal combo)
findings.description: If styles.badgeText uses brand.primary (#0D9488) as text colour on a white or light badge surface it achieves only 3.06:1, failing AA for normal-sized text; if the badge is a teal-tinted surface the ratio degrades even further.
findings.proposed_fix: Use Colors.light.tint (#0D9488) ONLY for large/bold text (≥18pt or bold ≥14pt); for normal-weight day labels use Colors.light.text (#0F172A, 17.85:1) or at minimum Colors.light.primaryDeep (#115E59, 5.87:1) on light surfaces.

findings.element: mutedText — time range in dark mode
findings.description: Colors.dark.textTertiary (#64748B) against the dark surface (#1E293B) yields a low contrast ratio that likely fails AA for normal text in dark mode even if the light-mode value passes.
findings.proposed_fix: In dark mode map mutedText to Colors.dark.textSecondary (#94A3B8, 5.27:1 vs #0F172A background) to guarantee AA compliance across both schemes.

findings.element: Badge container background (styles.badge) in dark mode
findings.background: unknown badge fill — may remain a light teal surface (#F0FDFA) in dark mode
findings.description: If styles.badge applies brand.primarySurface (#F0FDFA) as its background without a dark-mode override, the badge will appear as a bright light element on a dark screen, and any light text colour intended for dark mode will fail against it.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a dark-mode conditional to styles.badge so its background resolves to Colors.dark.surfaceRaised (#263548) or Colors.dark.surface (#1E293B), keeping text tokens consistent with the dark theme.

findings.element: AvailabilityLabel — no selected / unavailable state differentiation
findings.description: The component renders the same visual treatment regardless of whether the availability slot is active, inactive, or in a conflicted state; users cannot distinguish availability status from colour or contrast alone.
findings.proposed_fix: Add an optional 'status' prop ('available' | 'unavailable' | 'conflict') and conditionally apply border or background tokens: Colors.light.successSurface + Colors.light.success text for available, Colors.light.errorSurface + Colors.light.error text for conflict, and Colors.light.textTertiary with reduced badge opacity for unavailable.

findings.element: scheduler.styles — badge and badgeText styles defined externally
findings.foreground: unknown — defined in scheduler.styles, not referenced via Colors tokens in this file
findings.description: All colour decisions are deferred entirely to an external stylesheet with no token enforcement at the component level; if scheduler.styles contains hardcoded hex values they bypass the design token system and cannot be audited here.
findings.proposed_fix: Destructure colour values from useThemeColor() or the Colors token map inside the component (or pass them as props from a themed parent) so the accessibility contract is explicit and auditable at the component boundary.

findings.description: Secondary / muted text in compact badge components is commonly set below 14px, which removes the AA Large exemption (3:1) and requires the full 4.5:1 ratio; the current font size is not declared in this file.
findings.proposed_fix: Ensure styles.mutedText specifies fontSize ≥ 14 with fontWeight '700' (to qualify as AA Large at 3:1) or fontSize ≥ 16 for normal weight body text, and set lineHeight to at least 1.5× fontSize (e.g. lineHeight: 24 for fontSize: 16).

findings.description: Badge label text is frequently set at small sizes (11–13px) for compact UI; at these sizes AA Large exemptions do not apply and any brand-colour text that only reaches 3.06:1 will fail.
findings.proposed_fix: Set badgeText fontSize to ≥ 12 with fontWeight '700' at minimum (preferably ≥ 14px bold) and use a token with ≥ 4.5:1 contrast such as Colors.light.primaryDeep (#115E59, 5.87:1) rather than brand.primary.

findings.element: headerBackgroundColor prop — raw hex strings passed by callers at runtime
findings.description: The component accepts arbitrary dark/light hex strings for the header background with no type constraint or token enforcement, making it impossible to guarantee any contrast between the header image/icon content and the background at the call site.
findings.proposed_fix: Change the prop type to accept only keys of the Colors token object (e.g. keyof ThemeColors) or a predefined union of safe token pairs, and resolve the actual colour inside the component via Colors[colorScheme][tokenKey], ensuring callers cannot supply unchecked hex values.

findings.description: Because each colour mode value is independently supplied by the caller without validation, a header image or icon that achieves sufficient contrast in light mode may fall below 3:1 in dark mode (or vice versa) with no mechanism in this component to detect or correct the discrepancy.
findings.proposed_fix: Audit every call site of ParallaxScrollView to verify both headerBackgroundColor.light and headerBackgroundColor.dark yield ≥3:1 contrast against the headerImage content; add a DEV-mode warning (e.g. via a useEffect) that logs a contrast alert when an unchecked colour is detected.

findings.description: During the parallax scale animation (scale up to 2× on over-scroll) the header image is stretched and repositioned, potentially exposing edge regions or transparent areas of the image against the background colour where no contrast guarantee exists.
findings.proposed_fix: Ensure headerImage assets include a solid background fill or a scrim overlay (e.g. a semi-transparent ThemedView with backgroundColor: Colors[colorScheme].background at opacity 0.35) at the bottom edge to maintain legibility of any text or icon content within the header during animation extremes.

findings.description: No indicatorStyle prop is set on the Animated.ScrollView, so the scroll indicator colour is left to the OS default, which may be invisible or low-contrast against the ThemedView background token (#F8FAFC light / #0F172A dark).
findings.proposed_fix: Add indicatorStyle={colorScheme === 'dark' ? 'white' : 'black'} to the Animated.ScrollView to ensure the scroll indicator always has sufficient contrast against the themed background.

findings.element: content ThemedView — padding and gap layout
findings.description: The content area correctly inherits themed text and background tokens yielding excellent contrast, but the 32px padding and 16px gap provide no minimum line-height or font-size enforcement for children, so consumer components could render small or low-contrast text without triggering a warning.
findings.proposed_fix: Document in a PropTypes or TypeScript comment that children must use textStyle tokens from Colors and maintain a minimum font size of 16px with lineHeight ≥ 1.5× fontSize; consider exporting a ParallaxContentText helper component that enforces these defaults.

findings.description: While not a colour issue directly, the contentContainerStyle is defined as an inline object literal on every render, bypassing StyleSheet.create optimisation; if a background colour is ever added here inline it would escape token enforcement.
findings.proposed_fix: Move contentContainerStyle into the StyleSheet.create block (e.g. styles.scrollContent) with paddingBottom handled via a dynamic style merge, ensuring any future colour additions automatically go through the token review process.

findings.background: styles.bannerWarning (unknown surface — likely brand.warningSurface #FFFBEB light / #451A03 dark)
findings.description: textTertiary (#64748B) is at the absolute AA floor on white (4.35:1); on a warm amber surface like warningSurface the ratio drops below 4.5:1, and in dark mode the same token on #451A03 must be verified — the low-luminance amber surface likely pulls the ratio below AA for normal-sized body text.
findings.proposed_fix: Use Colors.light.textSecondary (#475569, 6.86:1) or Colors.light.text (#0F172A) for the description copy inside bannerWarning; in dark mode use Colors.dark.text (#F1F5F9) to guarantee contrast on the dark amber surface.

findings.foreground: styles.linkText (token unknown — likely Colors.tint #0D9488 light / #2DD4BF dark)
findings.description: If linkText resolves to brand.primary #0D9488 (3.06:1 on white), it already fails AA for normal text on white; on a slightly coloured warningSurface the ratio worsens further, and the interactive label will fail WCAG 1.4.3 in both modes.
findings.proposed_fix: Set linkText foreground to Colors.light.primaryDeep (#115E59, 5.87:1 on white) in light mode and Colors.dark.tint (#2DD4BF, 8.95:1 on dark bg) in dark mode; apply via useColorScheme conditional inside scheduler.styles.ts.

findings.element: bannerText inside actionBanner (success / error / default variants)
findings.description: The banner background colours for success and error states are defined in scheduler.styles.ts and not auditable here; if they use brand.success (#10B981, 2.88:1 for white text) or brand.error (#EF4444, 4.55:1 for white text) directly, the success banner will fail AA and the error banner will be borderline — this gap widens in dark mode if the surface lightens.
findings.proposed_fix: Ensure bannerSuccess background uses Colors.light.successSurface (#ECFDF5) with text token Colors.light.success (#15803D, 5.44:1); bannerError uses Colors.light.errorSurface (#FEF2F2) with Colors.light.error (#DC2626, 4.64:1). Mirror with dark-mode equivalents from Colors.dark.

findings.element: Pressable wrapping linkText (openSetup link inside bannerWarning)
findings.description: The Pressable has no pressed/focused visual state (no android_ripple, no style callback for pressed), making it impossible to perceive activation for keyboard and switch-access users.
findings.proposed_fix: Convert to `<Pressable style={({ pressed }) => [styles.linkText, pressed && styles.linkTextPressed]}>` and define linkTextPressed with opacity 0.7 or an underline + teal background tint to satisfy WCAG 2.4.11 focus appearance.

findings.element: bannerWarning / dismissibleBanner — no dismiss/close button visible
findings.description: The dismissible banner class is applied but no close affordance is rendered in this file; if the dismiss action is only available via the 'openSetup' link, users who want to defer setup have no keyboard-accessible way to collapse the banner.
findings.proposed_fix: Add an accessible close IconButton (×) with accessibilityLabel={t('common.dismiss')} and accessibilityRole='button', coloured with Colors.light.textSecondary on the warning surface to meet 3:1 icon contrast.

findings.description: Contrast is excellent (AAA) — flagged LOW as a positive confirmation; no change needed.
findings.proposed_fix: No change required; tokens are correct.

findings.element: subtitle ThemedText using styles.mutedText on page background
findings.description: textTertiary (#64748B) achieves only 4.35:1 on the Slate-50 page background — 0.15:1 below the AA 4.5:1 threshold for normal-sized body text; this is the minimum and leaves no ambient-light safety margin for outdoor mobile use.
findings.proposed_fix: Use Colors.light.textSecondary (#475569, 6.86:1) for subtitle/descriptor body copy, reserving textTertiary strictly for placeholder-exempt input hints.

findings.description: StatusBar style='auto' delegates tint resolution to the OS and may render light-on-light or dark-on-dark in edge cases (e.g. custom nav themes, modals with differing backgrounds), providing no guarantee that the status-bar icons meet the 3:1 non-text contrast requirement against the app background.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace style='auto' with explicit style={colorScheme === 'dark' ? 'light' : 'dark'} so status-bar icons are always the inverse of the app background, guaranteeing sufficient contrast in both modes.

findings.element: RootLayout loading gate (returns null while fonts load)
findings.description: Returning null during font load produces a blank screen with no loading indicator, which is invisible and inaccessible; users with slower devices see no feedback, and the abrupt content flash when fonts resolve can disorient users with vestibular or cognitive disabilities.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace the null return with a minimal accessible loading state, e.g. <View style={{ flex:1, backgroundColor: Colors.light.background }} accessible accessibilityLabel='Loading' /> or a themed ActivityIndicator using Colors.light.tint / Colors.dark.tint, so the screen is never fully blank.

findings.description: React Navigation's DefaultTheme and DarkTheme use their own hardcoded color values (e.g. background #fff, card #f5f5f5, text #1c1c1e) which are not aligned with the Horario design token palette; headers, bottom sheets, and modals spawned by the navigator may render with off-token colours that have not been audited for contrast.
findings.proposed_fix: Extend DefaultTheme and DarkTheme with Horario tokens: const HorarioLightTheme = { ...DefaultTheme, colors: { ...DefaultTheme.colors, background: Colors.light.background, card: Colors.light.surface, text: Colors.light.text, border: Colors.light.border, primary: brand.primary } } and the equivalent dark variant, then pass these to ThemeProvider to ensure all navigator-owned UI uses audited token colours.

findings.description: The component accepts arbitrary lightColor/darkColor strings from callers without any validation or documentation constraint, meaning any call site can inject a raw hex value that bypasses the design-token system and may silently fail contrast requirements.
findings.proposed_fix: Restrict the prop type to `keyof ThemeColors` (imported from constants/Colors) so only validated design tokens can be supplied, or add a JSDoc warning that caller-supplied values must be design tokens from Colors/brand and never raw hex strings.

findings.description: When neither lightColor nor darkColor is provided the component correctly falls back to the 'background' token, but there is no explicit defaultProps or inline comment documenting this contract, making it easy for a future maintainer to assume the default is white (#FFFFFF) in both modes and accidentally compose overlapping ThemedViews that collapse contrast in dark mode.
findings.proposed_fix: Add an inline comment or JSDoc: `// Defaults to Colors.[scheme].background — never hardcode a fallback hex at call sites` to make the contract explicit and prevent accidental dark-mode contrast regressions.

findings.description: The style array applies the token-derived backgroundColor first and the caller's style second, meaning any backgroundColor in the spread style silently wins and can introduce an un-audited surface colour; this creates a systemic risk for downstream contrast failures across every screen that uses ThemedView.
findings.proposed_fix: Either reverse the order to `[style, { backgroundColor }]` so the token always wins, or document explicitly that callers must never override backgroundColor directly and should instead use the lightColor/darkColor props — whichever matches the intended API contract.

findings.description: Skeleton bar colour #CBD5E1 is hardcoded rather than drawn from a design token, bypassing the token system and making dark-mode adaptation impossible — on a dark surface (#1E293B) the contrast is approximately 1.8:1, which is invisible.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a skeleton token to Colors (e.g. Colors.light.skeletonBase: '#CBD5E1', Colors.dark.skeletonBase: '#334155') and reference it via useColorScheme; replace both hardcoded values with the token.

findings.element: lineShort and lineLong skeleton bars in dark mode
findings.description: #CBD5E1 bars on the dark surface token (#1E293B) produce only ~1.8:1 contrast, making the skeleton shape imperceptible to users in dark mode.
findings.proposed_fix: In dark mode swap to Colors.dark.border (#334155) or a slightly lighter value such as #475569 (Slate 600) which gives ~2.5:1 — or preferably #64748B (Slate 500) at ~3.0:1 against #1E293B to meet the non-text 3:1 threshold.

findings.description: At the low end of the pulse (opacity 0.3) the effective bar colour blends toward white, dropping the perceived contrast to roughly 1.5:1 — the skeleton shape may be invisible to low-vision users even in light mode.
findings.proposed_fix: Raise the minimum opacity from 0.3 to at least 0.5, or widen the contrast of the base colour (e.g. use #94A3B8 Slate 400 at full opacity and pulse between 0.6 and 1.0) so the element remains visible at the animation nadir.

findings.description: The same hardcoded #CBD5E1 value is repeated for lineLong; both occurrences should be centralised into a single token reference to prevent future colour drift.
findings.proposed_fix: Extract the colour to a single local constant or token (e.g. const skeletonColor = colors.skeletonBase) and apply it to both lineShort and lineLong, eliminating the duplication.

findings.description: HapticTab wraps PlatformPressable without defining any pressed, focused, or disabled visual style overrides, delegating all state rendering to the parent navigator; if the navigator's default pressed ripple/overlay is insufficient (e.g. below 3:1 change in perceived colour) there is no fallback differentiation defined at this layer.
findings.proposed_fix: Pass an `android_ripple` prop and/or a `style` callback to PlatformPressable that applies a token-based pressed overlay (e.g. `backgroundColor: Colors[scheme].border` at reduced opacity) so pressed state is visually distinguishable at ≥3:1 across both light and dark themes.

findings.description: Dark mode icon passes AA non-text at 5.27:1, but the light mode icon token (#475569 at 6.86:1 vs white) is meaningfully stronger — the dark mode chevron may appear dimmer than intended in high-ambient-light outdoor conditions despite technically passing.
findings.proposed_fix: No immediate AA fix required; for AAA outdoor safety consider using Colors.dark.text (#F1F5F9) or Colors.dark.tint (#2DD4BF) as the icon color in dark mode to match the higher contrast of the light counterpart.

findings.element: headingFocused borderColor hardcoded to Colors.light.tint in StyleSheet.create
findings.description: The StyleSheet.create call for headingFocused hardcodes Colors.light.tint as borderColor, meaning in dark mode the focus ring will always use the light teal (#0D9488) against a dark background (#0F172A) where it renders at only ~6.88:1 — this actually passes, but the static reference means the style is disconnected from the theme system and could silently break if tokens change; additionally, the inline override on line 31 correctly reads Colors[theme].tint so the static fallback in the StyleSheet is a latent DARK_MODE_GAP.
findings.proposed_fix: Remove borderColor from styles.headingFocused in StyleSheet.create entirely (keep borderWidth, borderRadius, padding) and rely solely on the inline { borderColor: Colors[theme].tint } already applied in the style array on line 31.

findings.element: headingFocused style — static StyleSheet reference to Colors.light.tint
findings.description: styles.headingFocused is defined at module load time using Colors.light.tint, creating a hardcoded light-mode token that leaks into dark mode if the inline override is ever removed or reordered in the style array.
findings.proposed_fix: Define headingFocused without any color property: `headingFocused: { borderWidth: 2, borderRadius: 8, padding: 4 }` and supply borderColor exclusively via the runtime `{ borderColor: Colors[theme].tint }` inline style already present.

findings.element: TouchableOpacity collapsed vs expanded state — chevron rotation only
findings.description: The open/closed state is conveyed only by a 90-degree chevron rotation with no colour change or label update, which may be insufficient for users with cognitive or motion-sensitivity constraints (prefers-reduced-motion is not respected).
findings.proposed_fix: Add an accessibilityHint such as `accessibilityHint={isOpen ? 'Tap to collapse' : 'Tap to expand'}` and consider skipping the rotation transform when the user's system has reduced-motion enabled (via useReducedMotion or Animated with a duration of 0).

findings.description: The icon is 18px with a gap of 6px; the overall TouchableOpacity touch target height is determined by content only and may fall below the WCAG 2.5.5 recommended 44×44pt minimum on short titles.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `minHeight: 44` and `minWidth: 44` to styles.heading, or wrap the TouchableOpacity with `hitSlop={{ top: 12, bottom: 12, left: 12, right: 12 }}` to ensure an adequate touch target regardless of content height.

findings.element: Link (ExternalLink) — text colour inherited from parent/caller
findings.description: ExternalLink applies no explicit text colour, so contrast depends entirely on the call-site context; if rendered on a non-white or image background the ratio is unverifiable and could fail AA.
findings.proposed_fix: Accept an optional `color` prop defaulting to `Colors.light.tint` (#0D9488, 3.06:1 on white — AA Large) or preferably `brand.primaryDeep` (#115E59, 5.87:1) for inline body-text links, and apply it via `style={{ color }}` to guarantee AA compliance.

findings.description: No pressed, focused, or visited style is defined; users relying on visual focus indicators (keyboard or switch-access on web/native) receive no feedback that the link is interactive or activated.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a `style` prop that includes a focus/pressed variant, e.g. `pressed && { opacity: 0.7, textDecorationLine: 'underline' }` and on web ensure a visible `:focus-visible` outline using `Colors.light.borderFocus` (#0D9488).

findings.description: If a parent applies `Colors.light.tint` as the link colour without adapting for dark mode, the teal-on-dark-background ratio falls to ~3.06:1, failing AA for normal-weight body text.
findings.proposed_fix: Use `useColorScheme` to conditionally apply `Colors.dark.tint` (#2DD4BF, 8.95:1 on #0F172A) in dark mode instead of the light-mode primary teal.

findings.description: If styles.mutedText resolves to Colors.light.textTertiary (#64748B) without dark-mode branching, applying that same token on the dark surface (#1E293B) yields approximately 2.77:1, failing WCAG AA for normal-weight body text.
findings.proposed_fix: Ensure mutedText uses a themed colour hook so dark mode resolves to Colors.dark.textSecondary (#94A3B8, 5.27:1 on #1E293B) or Colors.dark.text (#F1F5F9); replace the static StyleSheet value with useThemeColor({ light: Colors.light.textTertiary, dark: Colors.dark.textSecondary }).

findings.description: If the 'subtitle' ThemedText variant maps to textSecondary in both modes the dark pairing (#94A3B8 on #1E293B) achieves 5.27:1 and passes, but if the variant maps to textTertiary (#64748B) in dark mode the ratio drops to ~2.77:1; the mapping should be verified to guarantee AA compliance in dark mode.
findings.proposed_fix: Confirm ThemedText type='subtitle' explicitly maps to Colors.dark.textSecondary (#94A3B8) or Colors.dark.text (#F1F5F9) in dark mode — never to the shared #64748B textTertiary token which fails on dark surfaces.

findings.element: subtitle ThemedText with styles.mutedText — light mode
findings.description: textTertiary (#64748B) at 4.35:1 sits just below the 4.5:1 AA threshold for normal-weight text; it is technically compliant only under the WCAG placeholder exemption but subtitle content is informational body text and should clear 4.5:1 with a safety margin for ambient-light legibility.
findings.proposed_fix: Use Colors.light.textSecondary (#475569, 6.86:1) for the subtitle; reserve textTertiary strictly for input placeholder text that disappears on focus.
